q: the other emigration there is a page here about port pirie because the family knew about port pirie. nobody knew about youngstown, johnstown, two american diasporas this archive did not know it had the other emigration there is a page here about port pirie because the family knew about port pirie. nobody knew about youngstown, johnstown, brooklyn, leadville, calumet or chicago - and the records are not scarce. they were simply never looked for. everything below was found in a single day on a commercial index, during a two-day trial. none of it is a claim of descent. it is a record of where people carrying these surnames went, what they gave as the village they had left, and who they named as kin - because that last field is what will eventually separate ours from not-ours. the zubrinici went twice, and the spelling tells you which search zubrinich and you get 191 records , almost all australian . search zubrinic - the unanglicised form - and you get a different 119 , almost all american. anybody searching one spelling has been missing the other entirely. under zubrinich - america a cluster at youngstown, ohio and johnstown, pennsylvania - steve, george, anton, pete, daniel, milan, anastasia - with wwi draft cards, censuses from 1905, a minnesota state census, a canadian border crossing at vermont, and an ivan zubrinich born 1888 living in brooklyn in 1930. for a surname carried by roughly 312 people on earth , a second emigration is not a coincidence. it is also not yet a connection. under zubrinic - lika, named these manifests give the village left behind : sumecica - franjo, 1910, leaving a wife franci and a brother ture otocac - georg 1903, "mjos" 1907 (sailing from fiume ) prozor - eva 1907, miko 1910, nikola 1911, anton 1911, mate 1911, miho 1912 sumecica houses 2 and 24, and prozor 46 and 50, are the oldest addresses in this archive. the frontier → prozor is emptying, and this archive stops just before it happens six people leave one village in five years - and the archive's own record of that village ends before any of them were born. who born sailed father named on the manifest kin met or left eva zubrinic 1880 1907 - bro-in-law joso gomercic miko zubrinic 1893 1910 ivan zubrinic uncle josef kostelac nikola zubrinic 1886 1911 sandro zubrinic bro-in-law jus oreskovic anton zubrinic 1891 1911 marco zubrinic - mate zubrinic 1867 1911 michael, per this archive wife roza · nephew stipan kostelac miho zubrinic - 1912 - bro-in-law nikola ladisic the gap this archive documents prozor 50 in detail - michael zubrinic, born 1826, and his seven children, nikola 1858 through franjo 1874. and then it stops. there is not one zubrinic born at prozor between 1875 and 1900 anywhere on this site. the manifests document precisely that missing generation, and name its fathers: ivan , sandro and marco . ivan is almost certainly ivan of prozor 50, born 1870 , whose own record also stops at his birth. sandro and marco are not here at all in any generation that could father a child in the 1880s - so prozor held at least two more zubrinic households than this archive knows of. and the in-laws are people we already hold. kostelac twice, oreskovic - fourteen of them here - and gomercic . the prozor emigrants married into the same families as the prozor people already in this archive. not proof of kinship. a very strong hint of it. and the kalanji went to the mining towns eighty-one migration records for a family this archive holds 216 people of - and it records no kalanj emigration at all . they sail 1891-1914, peaking in 1907, 1909 and 1913, into leadville, colorado ; calumet and houghton, michigan ; highland boy, utah ; duluth, chicago, akron, reno; and british columbia . the caution comes before the finding. split the given names and they fall in two: ivan, joso, mate, mile, miko, luka, ana, kata, marica - and bozo, duro, stevan, sava, todora, milica, jovan . the second column is not the naming pool of catholic klenovica. kalanj is also a serbian surname in lika , and the krajina sent its own emigration to exactly these towns in exactly these years. reading seven of the manifests gave four different home villages - brinje, plascica, kurjak, velgovica - none within forty kilometres of another. kalanj is a regional surname, not one household. of which exactly one matters. brinje is the parish this archive's own 1864 baptism names for the klenovica kalanji - s: Three German index cards, attached to Hedviga's husband in the family tree and never read, place him in a factory in Wür
q: the arolsen cards three german index cards, attached to hedviga's husband in the family tree and never read, place him in a factory in wur reutlingen and pfullingen, 1941-42 · surveyed 1950 the arolsen cards three german index cards, attached to hedviga's husband in the family tree and never read, place him in a factory in wurttemberg at the age of sixteen. the media sweep turned up three record images filed under ivan anton defranceski (1925-1995) from the arolsen archives - the international tracing service, the central archive of nazi persecution. the previous build of this archive listed them as an open question because nobody had looked at them. this page is what they say. the identification is firm. all three give the birth as 25 june 1925 at crikvenica - the same day and place as the 1951 yugoslav birth extract , which records the father of hedviga's children as "ivan defranceski, born 25.06.1925, crikvenica". one of the three cards writes 24 .6.25; that is a clerical slip against two other cards and a civil certificate. what the cards record name defranceski , forename written iwan and jvan - german renderings of ivan born 25 june 1925 , crikvenica - spelled grikvenica and cricvenica by two different clerks nationality kroatien-jugoslawien on one card; ? on another status led. - ledig , single. no wife and no children are entered on the insurance card, and every family line is blank. lodging pfullingen, brunnenstrasse 7 ; the reutlingen card gives the unterkunftsort simply as reutlingen employer 1 licht u. kraft , reutlingen - apparently the electricity and power undertaking. category hilfsarb. - hilfsarbeiter , unskilled labourer. 21 october 1941 - 16 january 1942. employer 2 a second reutlingen employer, same category. the name is written in an old german hand and this archive cannot read it confidently - it begins with what may be otto . 26 january 1942 - 28 november 194? - the final digit of the year runs into the column rule and is illegible. it is 1942 or 1944 , and the difference is ten months against nearly three years. insurance registration and deregistration numbers 8143 / 560 for the first post, 905 / 8614 for the second he turned sixteen in june 1941 and started at licht und kraft that october . the most important thing on these cards is what is missing three blank lines the 1950 municipal questionnaires exist precisely to establish what kind of worker a foreigner had been. three printed lines do that job. on both cards, all three are empty. wurde der arbeiter restlos entlohnt? "was the worker paid in full?" - blank dienstverpflichtet compulsorily assigned to service - blank freier arbeiter … seit free worker, since - blank so the record establishes that he was there and what he did , and is silent on the one question everybody asks first. this archive does not claim he was a forced labourer, and does not claim he went voluntarily. the boxes that would settle it were left empty by a german town clerk in 1950, five years after the fact. nor does the file title settle it. the collection is catalogued by the arolsen archives as "card file of persecutees in the later french zone and of french persecutees in other areas" (de its 2.3.3.1). that is the name of a zone-wide registration file compiled by the occupation authorities, not a finding about any individual in it. being in the file is not a finding of persecution. the second collection is the war time card file - registration cards, employees' record books, individual correspondence (02020201 os). the context, stated as context yugoslavia was invaded on 6 april 1941 and partitioned; the independent state of croatia was declared on 10 april 1941 under axis supervision, and sent workers to the reich under labour agreements. german recruitment of labour from the region hardened through late 1941 and 1942 as the war in the east stalled and the demand for workers became acute. ivan's first registration - 21 october 1941 - sits early in that sequence, before the openly coercive round-ups documented from 1942 onward. that is a reason to be careful in both directions: it does not make his going voluntary, and it does not make it forced. a sixteen-year-old from an occupied country working in a german power undertaking is not a free labour market in any case. reutlingen and pfullingen are neighbouring towns in wurttemberg. after 1945 they fell inside wurttemberg-hohenzollern , the french occupation zone administered from tubingen - which is why a croatian teenager's wartime employment was surveyed by french-zone municipalities in 1950 and why the insurance card is stamped document exploite . the cards krankenkasse membership and benefits card (mitglieder- und leistungskarte nr. 1), printed in fraktur. stamped diagonally document exploite by the french occupation authority. municipal questionnaire, reutlingen, kreis reutlingen, land wurttemberg - dated to 1950 with the annotation a.o.k. municipal questionnaire, stadt pfullingen, kreis reutlingen, wurttemberg-hohenzollern - stamped and signed 28 february 1950. where it sits in the life this is the earliest documented event in ivan defranceski's life after his birth, and it reframes the man hedviga married. 25 june 1925 born at crikvenica 21 oct 1941 aged 16 - begins at licht und kraft, reutlingen, as an unskilled labourer, lodging at brunnenstrasse 7, pfullingen 26 jan 1942 - 28 nov 194? a second reutlingen employer 1948 back in croatia: his daughter ladislava is born at crikvenica 17 dec 1951 his son ivan born at senj hospital; the birth extract gives his trade as electro-mechanic - which is what a boy who spent the war in a power undertaking might well become - and his nationality as italian 1954 that extract is drawn and translated for the supreme court of south africa 30 oct 1995 dies at senj. hedviga dies at johannesburg on the same date, six years later. what would settle the rest. the arolsen archives online collections hold these cards and may hold more under the same name - a direct search for defranceski, born 25.6.1925 would show the full file and resolve the illegible year. arolsen answers enquiries from families without charge. open questions →

q: blazevic the name the archive carries. eight generations, from a boy born about 1750 in a bunjevac settlement to a woman who died smokvica krmpotska, then senj blazevic the name the archive carries. eight generations, from a boy born about 1750 in a bunjevac settlement to a woman who died in johannesburg. 220 published people 1750 earliest birth year 4 distinct spellings in the tree where they are from every blazevic ancestor on the direct line before 1892 is placed at smokvica krmpotska , a village in the vinodol hills behind novi vinodolski - founded, like krivi put, by bunjevci krmpocani settled there by the military frontier between 1605 and 1647. the settlement → the move to town toma blazevic (1838-1907) is the hinge. he is born at house 114 in smokvica krmpotska and he dies at senj , a nadnicar - day labourer. the family comes off the mountain into a port town in the decades after that port stopped working. senj → his death entry, read the senj death register for 1907 (p.225, entry 60) gives him in full: 26 srpnja - july - 1907 , blazevic toma, nadnicar , udovac iza pok. tereze - widower of the late tereza - aged 69 , of tuberculosis , sacraments administered, buried at the cemetery of sv. vid on 28 july . he is not alone on that page. two entries above him a tobacco-factory worker of thirty dies of the same disease, three days earlier; three entries above, a coachman of twenty-four is entered as ustrieljen - shot - with the sacraments not administered. this is one week in one small town. house 114 is a zadruga the register identifies a household by its house number, and one number runs through this family. toma blazevic is born at br. 114, smokvica krmpotska in 1838, and is recorded there with terezija pecanic at the baptisms of ivan in 1882 and tonka in 1884 . in 1895 juraj appears in the same book as "jurko blazevic i tereza rod. zubrinic, selj. " , at smokvica kbr. 114 . this archive first read that as one household, and was wrong. a control document settles it: the baptism of frane blazevic, 2 august 1890 , puts pave blazevic i marija rod. tomljanovic at smokvica 114 as well - and that pavao is the son of luka , not of toma. three distinct nuclear families share the number across thirteen years. they join one generation up. luka blazevic and anton blazevic , toma's father, are both sons of ilija blazevic . pavao and toma are first cousins . smokvica 114 is therefore a zadruga - the south slav extended-family household, in which married brothers and cousins live under one number and hold the land in common. it is the characteristic form of the military frontier and of the bunjevac settlements . so the number places juraj inside ilija's kin-group , which is real and worth having, and it does not single out which man in that group was his father. what still would → the parish, at last the same entry gives his birthplace not as a village but as a parish : sv. jakov krmpote - st james of krmpote. that is the register that holds smokvica krmpotska, and therefore the book in which juraj , anton , ilija , grgica and matesa should be found. nobody has opened it. open questions → a caution about the surname blazevic is the 17th most common surname in croatia - 7,216 bearers there, 11,163 worldwide - and its densest counties are split-dalmatia, virovitica-podravina and osijek-baranja, none of which is this family's. shared surname is not evidence of shared descent here. the names → where they were s: Smokvica Krmpotska and Krivi Put are not ancient. They were settled on purpose, in living memory of the Ottoman wars, by
q: the bunjevci smokvica krmpotska and krivi put are not ancient. they were settled on purpose, in living memory of the ottoman wars, by why these villages exist at all the bunjevci smokvica krmpotska and krivi put are not ancient. they were settled on purpose, in living memory of the ottoman wars, by refugees the habsburgs planted on an empty mountain to hold it. two of hedviga's four grandparental lines - the blazevici of smokvica krmpotska and the prpici of krivi put - come out of villages in the senj hinterland that did not exist in 1600 . knowing that changes what it means to say the family is "from" there. who the bunjevci are the bunjevci are a catholic south slavic group whose homeland before the ottoman wars lay in the western balkan hinterland, around the krmpote district near zemunik behind zadar. the krmpotic clan - the largest of them - abandoned that territory under ottoman pressure between about 1465 and 1467 , and moved north and toward the coast. they are usually described in three branches: the dalmatian bunjevci, the danubian bunjevci who ended up around subotica in the backa, and the littoral-lika bunjevci. this family belongs to the third. 1605-1647 the planting of the senj mountain the first organised migration to the croatian littoral is dated to 1605 , when about fifty families from krmpote near zemunik were settled at lic near fuzine. further waves down to 1647 settled the hinterland of senj - ledenice, krmpote, krivi put and the senjska draga . the settlers brought the name of the district they had left: the new krmpote in the vinodol hills is named for the old krmpote behind zadar, and smokvica krmpotska - "smokvica of the krmpote people" - carries it in its surname. this was frontier policy, not accident. the habsburg military frontier needed a loyal, armed, catholic population on the empty ground behind senj. the settlers got land and grazing; the empire got a militia. the name of the road. the story told locally is that a bunjevac, asked which way some venetian fugitives had gone, answered that they had taken the crooked path - krivi put - and the district, until then called svetojakovski and then krmpotski , has been krivi put ever since. this archive records it as local tradition , which is what it is. what that means for this family krivi put 136 the prpici are recorded at a specific house: krivi put 136 . thirty-five people in this tree are born at that address, including antonija "tonka" prpic on 12 may 1859 , baptised three days later at krivi put with lucas and anna tomljanovic standing as godparents. house numbers are how the frontier registers worked. a settled family is its house number for a century at a time - which is why the same address can produce four generations. smokvica krmpotska, house 114 toma blazevic was born on 27 january 1838 at br. 114, smokvica krmpotska - br. for broj , number. his father anton , his grandfather ilija (b. c. 1790) and the two men above them are all placed in the same village. in 1835 krivi put was the seat of a captain's post under krmpote, with 98 houses and 1,246 people . that is the scale of the world these families were born into. how these households actually worked the zadruga at smokvica 114 the registers do not just place this family in a bunjevac village. they show it living in the characteristic household form of the frontier and the settlements - and this archive only saw it after reading a document meant as a control. 1838 toma blazevic born at br. 114, smokvica krmpotska 1882, 1884 toma and terezija pecanic , seljaci , at smokvica 114 - the baptisms of ivan and tonka 1890 pavao blazevic and marija tomljanovic at smokvica 114 - and this pavao is the son of luka , not of toma 1895 "jurko blazevic i tereza rod. zubrinic, selj. " at smokvica kbr. 114 - the baptism of marijan 1912 antonija's marriage names her parents as "†† toma i tereza blazevic, poljodjelci iz sela smokvica kbr. 114" luka and anton - toma's father - are both sons of ilija blazevic , born about 1790. so pavao and toma are first cousins , and three generations of ilija's descendants share one house number. that is a zadruga : the south slav extended-family household, in which married brothers and cousins live under one roof and one number and hold the land in common. it was the ordinary form of tenure in the military frontier , where a household - not a man - owed the regiment its service, and it survived in these settlements long after the frontier itself was abolished in 1881. what it cost this archive. the house number was read here as a household, and used as strong evidence that toma was juraj's father. it is not. it identifies a kin-group , and cannot say which man in it was whose father. what still could → and why it is invisible ten miles away the town does not count houses the village registers of krmpote and krivi put enter a house number against every child - smokvica 114 , krivi put 136 , klenovica 22 , povile 22 . the town register of senj does not. under the same printed column - mjesto obitavanja i kucni broj , place of residence and house number - a senj entry says simply "senj" . so the papici cannot be traced through a house the way the blazevici can, and a zadruga among them would be invisible even if it existed . that is a difference between a town and a village, not between two families - and it is worth knowing before concluding anything from the absence. the bunjevac identity is asserted here by place, not by document. no record in this tree calls anyone a bunjevac. what the records give is birth in villages that were founded by bunjevci and populated by them, bearing surnames - blazevic, prpic, tomljanovic, vukelic - that are standard in those settlements. that is a strong inference and it is offered as an inference. method →

and in these parishes the priest wrote both, joined them with a word, and underlined the join. this page exists because a question got a bigger answer than it asked for. question 5 asked whether antic and papic were one family or two, and whether papa was a surname or something else. the answer is that papa is a nadimak - a house by-name - and the surname it sits beside is antic. but the evidence turned out not to be about this family at all. reading the registers at full resolution in september 2026 found the same construction 17 times, across 11 surnames and 5 parishes , over 104 years and at least three different priests' hands. papa is one instance of a system. the tell the scribes underlined them 8 of the 17 phrases are underlined in the register itself . not the archive's emphasis - the priest's. that is what makes this a finding rather than a guess. a scribe who underlines antich papa , lonzarich franich and jellichich dictis juresina on his own pages is not writing down two surnames by accident. he is marking a convention he expects a later reader to need - and two hundred years later, that reader is this archive. where a connecting word is used it is vulgo , dictis , dicti , aliter , adoptatus - latin for otherwise , called , and in one case adopted . often there is no word at all and the two names simply run together. every phrase read year as written surname by-name where 1781 ex vincentio, et oliva smoyver, vulgo vukic, conjugibus baptism of ahn 53, 11 mar 1781, page 65; ark 3:1:3qs7-l99c-l998-5 smojver vukic karlobag 1806 marthae antich papa underlined baptism of ahn 24, 14 mar 1806 antic papa vrbnik or selce 1806 maria antich dudin underlined same page, 22 mar 1806, godmother antic dudin vrbnik or selce 1806 maria lonzarich franich underlined same page, 22 mar 1806, mother loncaric franic vrbnik or selce 1809 margarita jellichich dictis juresina underlined baptism of ahn 25, 22 mar 1809 jellicic juresina selce 1809 vincentii lonzarich hel dicti underlined same entry, godmother's husband loncaric hel selce 1835 josephum antich papa underlined marriage of ahn 24 × 25, domus 51 antic papa selce 1835 euphemia antich, aliter papa his sister, same day, domus 80 antic papa selce 1835 marca badrovich aliter bagatello same opening, bride badrovic bagatello selce 1835 josephum dudich aliter antich underlined same opening, a different joseph antic dudic antic selce 1835 josepho franich aliter lonzarich same opening, witness franic loncaric selce 1835 marcus oreskovich, adoptatus sekula underlined baptism at dubrava 29, 8 sep 1835 oreskovic sekula otocac 1835 franciscum penes aliter paschul same opening, groom penes paschul selce 1835 lucia puxich aliter lonzarich same opening, bride puzic loncaric selce 1838 josephi antich papa baptism of ahn 12, domus 51 antic papa selce 1842 vincentius antich, aliter dudich death, 29 jan 1842, aged 63 antic dudic selce 1885 juraj papa marriage of ahn 6, p.192 no.5 - the by-name alone, surname gone papic papa senj what it is for a village where forty households share nine surnames cannot be run on surnames. the by-name is the thing that tells which antic you mean. it is the same job the house number does at smokvica, and the same job the patronymic does at otocac - ivo blazevic sin tomin against ivo blazevic sin matin , two men of one name told apart by their fathers. three devices, one problem. and at grizane in 1738 the census does it a fourth way: juraj car vulin , matij car jurisin , lovro car mikulin - of vule, of juraj, of mikula - and one household identified purely by marriage, mikula … blaskovicha zet , blaskovic's son-in-law. why it matters beyond one question a by-name can eat a surname the antici are the proof. watch the same family across five documents: 1806 antich papa - surname first, by-name second, underlined 1835 josephum antich papa - still both, underlined 1835 euphemia antich aliter papa - his sister, the join spelled out 1838 josephi antich papa - still both, at his son's font 1885 juraj papa - the surname is gone by 1885 the priest at senj writes only the by-name, and every descendant after him is written papic . the house name became the family name in three generations , and the registers caught it happening. the warning in it. if a by-name can replace a surname, then two records of one family can disagree about its name without either being wrong - and two families can look like one because they share a by-name. any match made on a surname in these parishes is weaker than it looks. that is the rule the duplicate finder is built around, and this is where it comes from. checked 14 september 2026 does this matter to the other six archives? six sibling archives share a family tree with this one. on the names, no. of the ten surnames carrying a by-name here, exactly one - papic - appears in any sibling archive's surname list, and that archive is this one. on the method, quite possibly yes. the defranceschi archive covers istria · kvarner · carnia - and kvarner is the same coast: krk, vinodol, the parishes whose priests wrote aliter and underlined it. a convention this consistent across ten surnames and three parishes is unlikely to stop at the edge of one family's records. recorded as a negative result rather than left as an open loop. nothing has been changed in another archive on the strength of it.

q: who they married a pedigree takes one person per generation and drops the rest. look instead at who a family marries repeatedly and diffe five families the zubrinici and blazevici kept marrying who they married a pedigree takes one person per generation and drops the rest. look instead at who a family marries repeatedly and different things appear: a german name inside the military frontier, a krivi put family that married the blazevici nine times, six marriages into one otocac household, and an adoption working its way through three generations of surnames. correction, 13 september 2026 sojat is a family, not a by-name this archive recorded sojat as the by-name the tree attaches to one blazevic household - reading it as a nadimak like papa on the antici . that was wrong. the sojati are a krivi put family with fifteen people, dates and a place of their own . marko sojat, born 19 april 1801 at krivi put, died 4 february 1871 , with five children whose births and deaths are all recorded - simun 1819, marija 1825, matija 1828, mate 1830, martin 1831. one of them is entered at a place called sojat dol 54 - a valley named after the family. and they married the blazevici nine times. marija sojat 1825-1896 m. anton "kljapo" blazevic · 9 children kate sojat b. 1844 m. joso blazevic marija sojat m. antona blazevic · 4 children mare sojat m. antone blazevic · 2 children marija sojat m. mile blazevic nikola sojat b. 1878 m. kata blazevic maria sojath 1823-1891 m. domianus perpic · 4 children ivka sojat m. dametar perpic ivan sojat m. ivka prpic so blazevic (sojat) in the tree is almost certainly a household known by the family it married - which is how a nadimak is born, and the opposite of what this archive said. the mechanism was right and the direction was backwards. untersinger - a german name inside the frontier seven people, and unusually for this archive they are a complete three-generation household with dates : lucas untersinger → george, born 25 march 1787, died 1848 , married to helena → five children, rosalia 1802, ana 1807-1845 , michael 1810-1840, lucia 1827, eva 1839. ana untersinger married elias "ilija" zubrinic , and they both died in 1845 , leaving seven children - the event question 4b suspects was an epidemic in lika. a german surname in lika is not an accident. the military frontier was administered from vienna and its officer, forestry and clerical grades were staffed from across the monarchy. a zubrinic marrying an untersinger in the 1820s is a frontier family marrying into the administration of the frontier - which fits the six salaried posts this family held. what would test it: the otocac registers for george untersinger (1787) and his father lucas, and whether either is entered with a rank or an office. if the untersingers arrived as frontier staff rather than as settlers, the entry will say so. but the household does not hold together checked against itself on 13 september 2026, this "complete three-generation household" contradicts itself twice. george is born in 1787 and rosalia in 1802 - he would be fifteen. and helena is born in june 1788 and eva in 1839 , making her fifty-one. neither is impossible; both together, in a family of seven, are a warning. the likeliest reading is that rosalia and eva are not george and helena's children at all - that a generation is compressed, as it is in several other households here . which matters for the argument above, because the dates are the only reason to place the marriage "in the 1820s". not one untersinger is published on this site - which is why nobody looked at the household as a household. to be exact about it, one of the two was already caught: helena bearing eva at fifty-one is on the contradictions page as a mother-too-old. the other, george at fifteen, sits just under that check's threshold of thirteen and was never flagged at all. added 13 september 2026 butorac - a household that stood godparent twice and is not in the tree reading the godparent column for the first time turned up jandre and marija butorac standing for two of toma blazevic's children at smokvica 114 - ivan in 1882 and tonka in 1884 . the 1882 entry names her explicitly as "marija butorac, supruga jandrina" , jandre's wife. standing twice, two years apart, is not a courtesy. it is a standing relationship between two households , and it is the kind of tie that marriage records and house numbers usually hide. neither of them is in this tree. the only butorac in the entire export is margareta butorac , born 4 march 1870 at ledenice, who married franjo kalanj - a different family, a different village, and too young to be either godparent. so jandre and marija are known to this archive from one column of one register and from nowhere else. what would test it: the sv. jakov krmpote marriage register for a jandre butorac, and the house number his household is entered under. if it is near 114, the tie is neighbourhood; if it is far, it is more likely kin - and the mother of these children is a pecanic , whose own people are barely in this archive either. added 13 september 2026 katnic - seventeen people at crikvenica, none published seventeen katnici sit in the export, running 1722 to 1950 , and almost all of them at crikvenica - which is where ana kalanj's grave is, and where the defranceski side of hedviga's household buried its dead. none is published here, because katnic is not one of the nine surnames. they surface only as a contradiction: luka katnic , born 1722 and died 10 december 1755 , is entered as the father of margaretha (1757) and magdalena (1768) - thirteen years after his death. that is one of the twenty , and it is a wrong join rather than a bad date. noted rather than pursued. they belong to the crikvenica material, which is mostly the sister archive's, and this page exists to say where the edges of this one are. kostelac - six marriages into one household fifteen people, and six of them married zubrinici : stephanus married barbara zubrinic; maria kostelacz, juliana kostelacz and maria kostelac each married a joannes zubrinic; martinus married francisca zubrinic; michael married lucia zubrinic. a seventh, mande kostelac, married a sekula . two consequences. three women of one surname married men of one name - which is exactly the soil in which the michael zubrinic confusion grew, and a warning about how little a name identifies here. and one couple is in the tree twice. stephanus kostelacz + barbara zubrinic and stipan kostelac + bare zubrinic are the same marriage under latin and croatian forms of both names - and both versions carry a daughter born 19 april 1849 , entered once as lucia and once as luce . oreskovic and sekula - an adoption, and why question 4d was hard the 1835 otocac baptism of maria catharina enters her father as marcus oreskovich, adoptatus sekula . the tree explains it: marcus oreskovic, born 18 april 1809, is the son of vitus sekula . he was born a sekula and carries oreskovic. then he married a sekula - lucia, born 14 april 1815, daughter of a different sekula household - and two of their sons carry both surnames at once : franciscus oreskovic oreskovic sekula (1844) and petrus oreskovic oreskovic sekula (1846). born one name, living under another, married back into the first, and passing both to his children. that is the same machine as antich papa becoming papic - a surname changing hands over three generations - running in a different family at the same time. the names → and it explains why question 4d was so hard. the zubrinici married oreskovici at least four times : magdalena oreskovic (b. 1796) married nicolaus zubrinic; francisca (b. 1815) married paulus zubrinic; maria catharina (b. 1835) is given to michael; antonius oreskovic married helena zubrinic. "a maria oreskovic married to a michael zubrinic" was never going to identify anybody - the two families had been marrying each other for half a century. question 4d → kosina - a slovenian merchant who walked over the mountains the family anka blazevic married into in 1919, and the family that lost pavao in the 1943 raid , are not croatian. their senj marriage of 12 january 1888 gives martin kosina's origin as kranjska, zupa sv. martin kod krainburg - carniola, the parish of st martin near kranj , in what is now slovenia . he was a trgovac , a merchant, and 47 when he married the 30-year-old angjelika boras , a silica - seamstress. the entry names only his mother , gertruda kosina, posjednica - a woman of property, with a german name and no husband recorded. two generations later the family was senj's. martin's sons pavao and antun married four days apart in november 1919, both entered trgovac like their father; pavao was killed in the air raid of 8 october 1943; and the grave that carries him was restored by the family in 1991 with a priest's cross against it. senj, 1943 → the boras side held office: josip boras, gradski strazar - city guard - and the witness ivan boras, kr. pomorske straze nadstrazar , senior officer of the royal maritime guard. what these families have in common none of them is on the direct line. all four change what the direct line means . repetition is the signal. nine sojat marriages, six kostelac, four oreskovic. a single marriage tells you two people met; nine tells you two villages were one community. names move between families. sojat becomes a blazevic by-name; sekula becomes an oreskovic surname and then both; papa becomes papic. three separate instances of one mechanism , and this archive has now caught all three. and it is why identification keeps failing. when four oreskovici marry four zubrinici, a name and a surname identify nothing at all. what cannot be true →

s: A duplicate is not a mystery to be solved. It is one person counted as two, and it quietly inflates every number this ar
q: the same person, twice a duplicate is not a mystery to be solved. it is one person counted as two, and it quietly inflates every number this ar 23 duplicates confirmed, 28 rejected the same person, twice a duplicate is not a mystery to be solved. it is one person counted as two, and it quietly inflates every number this archive publishes about itself. finding them is easy. not over-finding them turned out to be the hard part. this check began as a zubrinic-only test and that was the mistake. run across all 1282 published people it finds the same disease in four families - and the first version of it was badly wrong , in a way worth showing rather than quietly fixing. what the first run claimed, and why it was wrong matching on surname, given name and birth year, the tool reported 42 duplicate groups holding 47 surplus records . that number is nonsense. most of those pairs are two different people who share a name - which is the one error this archive has warned about on every other page, since it holds eighteen ivan blazevici and refuses to auto-link names anywhere for exactly that reason. having written the warning, i walked into it. two tests fixed it. different parents means different people. nicolaus zubrinic, born at otocac in 1834, is the son of michael in one record and of lucas in the other - and he is ahnentafel 10 , a direct ancestor. without that test this page would have announced that this archive's own great-great-grandfather was a duplicate. and two death years means two people : antonius kalanj of klenovica 22, born 1868, is entered as dying in 1868 and in 1873. that is not one boy twice. it is a necronym - a dead child's name given to the next baby, which these families did constantly. with both tests the count falls from 42. the refinements below then bring it back up to 23 , because a test that is too strict throws away real duplicates as surely as a loose one invents them. comparing names is harder than it looks three further corrections were needed, and two of them came from outside the data - one from a photograph of a grave, one from noticing what was in the father's slot. the problem the case the rule a nickname in one record and not the other marijan cigo kalanj and marijan kalanj match given names by containment , not equality parents' names spelled differently michael vs michaelis / michael / miho compare parent names as sets, asking whether they overlap a short form and a full name for one parent mare vs marija · anton vs antona fold the short forms this region actually uses, and collapse doubled letters - phillipus and philippus are one man a sorting label standing in the father's slot jure zubrinic vs brothers of casparus (it seems) ignore bucket parents entirely - a label is not a father two spellings of one name, disjoint as tokens kate vs katalyn zubrinich where the full birth date, birth place and both parents agree, a shared three-letter prefix is enough a whole family duplicated in parallel lovro and lovre kalanj, each with their own ana, ivan and marijan allow one character of difference in a parent's name and the last was forced by reading the rejections. going through all thirty-two by hand - which had never been done - showed the parent test failing on the commonest thing in these registers. mile blazevic is in the tree three times , and the three entries give his parents as antona blazevic & marija sojat , antone blazevic & mare sojat , and anton kljapo blazevic & marija sojat . that is one couple written three ways, and the check called it three families. mare is not a variant spelling of marija. it is a different word for the same woman - and this archive has a whole page about exactly that. the same knowledge now sits in the tool: a short list of the short forms these registers actually use, plus a rule that collapses doubled letters, because phillipus and philippus are two substitutions apart and no single-edit test will ever join them. five groups came back, including a lucia and two magdalenas. and one was forced by a south australian birth index. this archive held kate zubrinich and katalyn zubrinich as two women - identical in birth date, birth place, death date, death place and both parents - and this check walked straight past them, because "kate" and "katalyn" are disjoint tokens rather than one inside the other. a findmypast search of the south australian births settled it: one registration in 1886, at port pirie, for a kate , and no katalyn anywhere in 176 records of that surname. one woman. the last of those was forced by a gravestone . a photograph of a grave at klenovica names lovro kalanj 1906-1965, ana kalanj 1919-1971, ivan kalanj 1942-1996, marijan kalanj 1944-2009 - one family, four people. the tree holds all four twice , and because the duplicated parents are spelled lovro in one copy and lovre in the other, the parent test rejected the children as different people. the stone said otherwise and the stone was right. which is the useful lesson: a parent-agreement test fails precisely when the parents are themselves duplicated. it is a good test and it is not a complete one. what survives the tests by confidence same day 7 same year and place 8 same year only 8 rejected 28 by family zubrinic 12 kalanj 5 blazevic 5 prpic 1 same day - q: the frontier one latin word in an 1834 baptismal entry - confiniarius - puts hedviga's grandmother's people inside the habsburg milit otocac, sumecica, prozor the frontier one latin word in an 1834 baptismal entry - confiniarius - puts hedviga's grandmother's people inside the habsburg military frontier, and changes what kind of family they were. the zubrinici are the rarest name in this archive and, until the otocac register was read, the least explained. the family tree gives tereza zubrinic one occupation - domacica , housewife - and her father and grandfather none at all. the register gives the household a legal status instead. 1834, januarii die 24ᵃ, ottocsatii - nicolaus , filius legitimus, catholicus . conditio: confiniarius, ex pago shumechia n⁰ 24 . parents michael xubrinich and maria uxor ejus nata oreskovich . what a confiniarius was the military frontier - vojna krajina , militargrenze - was a belt of territory the habsburgs administered not as a province but as a standing army . a frontiersman held his land from the emperor on condition of hereditary military service. he was not a serf and not quite a free peasant: he was a soldier who farmed, in a household that owed a man to the regiment. otocac had been a frontier captaincy since 1553 . in 1619 a body of uskoks displaced from senj moved inland to otocac and built the fortica - so the two towns at the two ends of this family's map are joined by the same dispersal. under maria theresa otocac was raised to the headquarters of a regiment: one of the four of the karlovac generalate , beside ogulin, slunj and lika. so when the priest writes confiniarius in 1834 he is not describing a job. he is recording which legal order the household belonged to - and by then the otocac regiment had existed for some seventy years. the frontier was not abolished until 1881 , within tereza's own lifetime. three zubrinic households, three offices the 1834 entry names three of them in four lines, and every one holds a post. the father michael xubrinich - confiniarius , of sumecica no. 24 the godfather petrus, son of franciscus xubrinich - vigiliarum ma[gister] , master of the watch , and pensionatus : a man drawing a pension, which means a career and a rank the godmother maria, wife of joannes xubrinich , silvarum custos in shumechia - forest warden of sumecica and the forestry is not a one-off. the tree records exactly one occupation across all 422 of its zubrinici, and it is "forest ranger" - held by joannes zubrinic, born 19 june 1837 , three years after the entry above. two generations, the same woodland office. why forests mattered here. frontier woodland was military property : the timber was the empire's, and guarding it was a salaried, uniformed, appointed post - not agricultural work. a silvarum custos is a small official of the state. the villages otocac the regimental town in the gacka valley, inland from senj across the velebit. 53 people in this tree are born or die here - the single largest zubrinic place. sumecica two house numbers, two centuries apart in the record: toma zubrinic , born 1768 at sumecica 2 , and michael's household at sumecica 24 in 1834. the name is from suma - forest . and the hungarian gazetteers say what it was. the helysegnevtar of 1913 counts 200 people there - beside otocac town's 2,676 and otocko staroselo's 423 - and degen's flora velebitica (1936) calls it a hausergruppe , a group of houses south-west of otocac, with a ponor at its foot that runs turbid when the lika floods. two hundred people is roughly twenty-five households - which is why the parish census, listing seven or eight, cannot be the whole village . on 14 september 2026 the two numbers stopped being separate. michael's son nicolaus , baptised into house 24 in 1834, is registering his own children in 1856 and 1858 at sumecica n° 2 - read off the page, in the conditio column of both entries. either he left his father's zadruga for the other house, or the man at house 2 is a different nicolaus. the status animarum was read the same day to decide it, and it cannot - all five sumecica openings hold dasovici, orehovici, stabincici and janezici, and no zubrinic, no domus 2 and no domus 24 . the baptism registers of 1846-1858 are the instrument instead : their conditio column writes the household out in full. prozor five kilometres south-east of otocac, on the site of roman arupium . seven children of one household are registered at prozor 50 between 1858 and 1874 - nikola, kata, georgius, magdalena, mate, ivan, franjo, to michael zubrinic and marija rogic. following the rarest name out of croatia the line that reached port pirie the australian zubrinichs can now be traced back three generations from the emigrant - and their story turns out to be the forestry family. casparus 1767-1829 "kasper / gaspar zubrinic xubrinich", born 14 january 1767; married helena (1765-1831), herself recorded under the surname zubrinic elias "ilija" 1806-1845 born 10 july 1806; married ana untersinger (1807-1845) - a german surname in lika , which the frontier's officer and administrative class would explain. both died in 1845 , leaving seven children between about one and fifteen. joannes b. 19 june 1837 forest ranger. eight years old when his parents died. married kata brajkovic on 12 january 1859 ivan / john 1860-1930 born the year after that wedding; reached port pirie, south australia about 1884, and from his first child in 1885 every descendant is registered zubrinich . port pirie → both parents in one year. elias and ana untersinger are both given 1845. two adults of thirty-eight and thirty-nine dying in the same year, in lika, in the 1840s, suggests an epidemic or a famine rather than coincidence - but the tree gives no dates, no causes and no source, and this archive has not looked. open questions → a fourth office, and a fourth zubrinic the foresters keep appearing the otocac baptismal register for 1835 - the next book along - produces another one. standing as godfather at an entry that september is stephanus xubrinich , entered as of the centuria ottocsana and sylvarum custos . 1834 joannes xubrinich , silvarum custos in shumechia 1835 stephanus xubrinich , of the otocac company, sylvarum custos b. 1837 joannes zubrinic - "forest ranger" , the only occupation the tree records for any of its 422 zubrinici and a fifth office, from 1845. the godmother at the baptism of josephus zubrinic on 16 march 1845 is entered as maria zubrinic, mulier custodis carcerum - wife of the keeper of the gaol . not a forester this time, but the same thing in kind: a salaried post in the frontier administration, held by a zubrinic, recorded only because somebody stood as a godparent. six posts, four generations, one surname - this is what the family did year who post 1834 petrus, son of franciscus vigiliarum magister pensionatus - retired master of the watch , drawing a pension 1834 joannes sylvarum custos in shumechicza - forest guard 1835 stephanus sylvarum custos of the centuria ottocsana - forest guard of the otocac company 1845 the wife of a zubrinic mulier custodis carcerum - wife of the keeper of the gaol b. 1837 joannes forest ranger - the only occupation the tree records for any zubrinic at all 1910 nikola kontrolor gradske dace - controller of the municipal excise , at senj read down that column and it is not a run of coincidences. it is an occupation. three of the six are forest posts, which is what a frontier regiment needed on wooded karst and what it paid for. one is the watch. one is the gaol. and the last, 1910 , is twenty-nine years after the military frontier was abolished - the same family still in salaried public service , now municipal rather than imperial. which makes what happened to the other side of this descent sharper. while the zubrinici were guarding forests and counting excise, the blazevici at smokvica 114 were seljaci and then nadnicari , and the papici went from dominus at karlobag to nadnicar at senj in three generations. two of hedviga's four families held office; two lost everything. they meet in her. every one of these six comes out of a godparent column or an occupation field - not one is recorded because somebody wrote the man's own life down. six posts from about thirty pages read → four men and one household of one rare surname, in one small district, holding salaried imperial office across at least two generations. this is what the family did. the tree, which records none of it, gives tereza zubrinic one word - domacica , housewife - and her forebears nothing. a correction to this archive's own direct line the mother who was born after her son this archive published maria catharina oreskovic as the wife of michael zubrinic and the mother of nicolaus , with a birth date of 8 september 1835 . nicolaus was born 24 january 1834 . she is twenty months younger than her son. the document settles it rather than rescuing it. the scan attached to her in the tree is a real entry and it is hers - otocac baptisms, 1835, entry 41: 1835, septembris die 8ᵛᵃ, ottocsitii - maria catharina , filia legitima, catholica . conditio: confinarius ex pago dubrava n⁰ d. 29 . parents: marcus oreskovich, adoptatus sekula , et lucia uxor ejus nata sekula . her parents in that entry are exactly the two the tree gives her - marcus oreskovic and lucia sekula . so the transcription is right and the attachment is wrong: a real maria catharina oreskovic of dubrava has been married to the wrong man and given somebody else's child. nicolaus's own 1834 entry names his mother as "maria uxor ejus nata oreskovich " . so an oreskovic she was - just an earlier one, born perhaps around 1810, and still unidentified. what this costs seven published ancestors hang below this join - maria catharina herself, her parents marcus and lucia, and the four sekulas above them. those people are real and their records are real. what is not shown is that they belong to this family. a second sign the same household in the tree lists "nikola zubrinic, b. 1880" as a sibling of nicolaus, born 1834 - a gap of forty-six years. where one attachment has slipped, others usually have. left standing the rest of the line is untouched: michael, nicolaus and tereza are joined by the 1834 register and by the 1920 marriage entry . what would fix it. the marriage of michael zubrinic and a maria oreskovic in the otocac registers, some time before 1834 - which would name the right woman and her father. until then this archive marks the oreskovic-sekula branch disputed and keeps it visible rather than deleting it, because a wrong join is itself a finding. method → the honest state of it 422 records, 90 loose ends, and an alphabet the zubrinic material in this tree is not one family . it is 422 records resolving into 90 loose ends - 90 people with no recorded zubrinic parent - which means the research has gathered the name without yet joining it up. our line descends from an unnamed "zubrinic" node with 731 descendants in the tree - the largest fragment - through toma (1768, sumecica 2) , michael (1811) , nicolaus (1834) and tereza (1867) . the australian line hangs above casparus on a node whose name , in the tree, is "brothers of casparus (it seems) zubrinic" . that is not a person. it is a researcher's working guess, written into the structure. therefore the two lines are not joined by anything. casparus (b. 14 january 1767) and toma (b. 1768) are born a year apart , in the same small frontier district, into a surname held today by about 312 people on earth . they are very probably close kin. probably is not shown. what would join them. the otocac parish registers of the 1760s , for the baptisms of casparus (14 january 1767) and toma (1768) - two entries on nearby pages, which would either name one father or two. why the placeholder nodes are dropped from this build →

and one of them belongs to a man who is not buried in it. two further graves, found since, say something consistent about what a stone is good for and what it is not. the blazevic plot, senj. neighbouring stones read vukelic, tomljanovic, bezjak and rogic - kata ✳ 1924 † 2007 · leo ✳ 1920 † 2008 rod. - rodena , "born", the croatian equivalent of nee . the stone therefore records milka's maiden name, papic - and not the vukelic name she married under in 1920 . why this photograph matters more than any other here it corroborates the account of oto's death oto blazevic ✳ 1923 † 1945 is on this stone. the family record carries two irreconcilable accounts of how he died - a snakebite, and the war in slavonia - and the second one, from nives blazevic , said this: …he died in the war somewhere in slavonia, his grave is unknown, so they put his name in his grandmother's and grandfather's grave - and now leo is there, and katica . the stone shows exactly that . oto's name is on the family plot; and the later plaque below carries leo (1920-2008) and kata - katica - (1924-2007), added afterwards, precisely as she described. one wrinkle resolves easily. nives calls it "his grandmother's and grandfather's grave", but the names on it are oto's parents . nives blazevic was born in 1953 : ljubomir and milka were her grandparents. she is describing the grave from her own position in the family, which is what people do. what this does and does not prove. it does not prove he died in slavonia. it proves that the person who said so knew this grave in detail - including who was added to it half a century later - and that the family commemorated oto somewhere other than a grave of his own. that is real corroboration of the witness, and it moves the snakebite account into second place. the brother → and it contradicts the register the stone gives ljubomir's birth as 1891 . the 1920 marriage register , written in his lifetime from his baptismal certificate, gives 1 march 1892 . this archive follows the register. it is a useful reminder in a family whose evidence is mostly stone and memory: a gravestone is a secondary source . it is cut after the fact, paid for by the bereaved, and carved by someone who never met the person. added 13 september 2026 two more graves, and the same lesson twice when that last paragraph was written it rested on one stone. sweeping the family's photo library turned up two more, in two more cemeteries - and one of them repeats the error exactly, while the other corrects the tree. crikvenica. ana de. franceschi ✻19 ix 1863 ✝28 v 1936, her husband josip, ruza jarmacki rodena defranceschi 1903-1939, and pepe, toni and bozica below. klenovica. lovro kalanj 1906-1965, ana kalanj 1919-1971, ivan kalanj 1942-1996, marijan kalanj 1944-2009 - a father, a mother and two sons. crikvenica gets a birth date wrong, exactly as senj does the stone gives ana de franceschi, born 19 september 1863 . her baptism survives and does not agree: anno domini 1864 , no. 2 - anna, legitima, josephus kalanj et rosalia nata perkovic ejus uxor , at klenovica n° 22 , born 3 january 1864 and baptised three days later. the death on the stone, 28 may 1936, is exactly right; the birth is out by three and a half months. so both stones this archive can test get the birth wrong and the death right - which makes sense. the death is what the family had just lived through. the birth is what somebody remembered, seventy years later. every name on the crikvenica stone is in the tree read against the record it resolves into one household over three generations, and the dates agree throughout: on the stone in the tree who ana de. franceschi ✻19 ix 1863 ✝28 v 1936 ana kalanj , 3 jan 1864 - 29 mar 1939, m. miro jarmacky their daughter ant… 1890 · ursula 1895 ante defranceski, b. 20 jan 1890, and ursula kovacina, 1895-1975 their son and his wife pepe 1911-1980 · bozica 1911-1994 josip petar "pepe" defranceski, 1911-1980, and bozica blaskovic grandson and his wife toni 1937-1984 anton "braco" defranceski, 16 nov 1937 - 17 jan 1984 great-grandson only one of the seven is published here. this archive publishes nine surname groups and defranceski is not among them, so the stone is almost entirely the sister archive's material - reached, as it happens, through a kalanj girl from klenovica who married into it. and reading it caught a fault in the tree. bozica blaskovic is entered as born 3 december 1911 and dying 18 may - the same day and month as her husband pepe, in both cases. two people do not share a birthday and a death-day. her years , 1911 and 1994, match the stone; the days and months have been copied across from his record. she is not published here, so this is noted rather than corrected - but it is worth the sister archive's attention. klenovica corrects the tree instead the four names on the kalanj stone are all in this archive - and all four are in it twice . because the duplicated parents are spelled lovro in one copy and lovre in the other, the duplicate check rejected the two sons as different people. the photograph is what overruled it: one family, one plot, four names. the same person, twice → a stone is a poor witness to a birth and a good witness to a household. it was cut by people who knew exactly who was buried together.

s: Hedviga “Seka” Blažević was born in a dying port on the Adriatic and died seventy-five years later on the Highveld, havi
q: hedviga hedviga "seka" blazevic was born in a dying port on the adriatic and died seventy-five years later on the highveld, havi senj 1926 - johannesburg 2001 hedviga hedviga "seka" blazevic was born in a dying port on the adriatic and died seventy-five years later on the highveld, having crossed a world war, a country that stopped existing, and two continents. she is the reason this archive exists, and she is also its best-documented person: a birth at senj on 3 august 1926 , a marriage into the defranceski family, three children, an immigration from zimbabwe in april 1975 , a second marriage to a sephardic jew from rhodes, and a death at johannesburg on 30 october 2001 with the cause written down plainly. what the record gives born 3 august 1926, senj father ljubomir "ljubo" blazevic (1892-1966), mornar - sailor mother milka lucia papic (1886-1971) - tobacco-factory worker at twenty-one, widow at twenty-eight, supervisor by the end siblings leo (1920-2008), karmela "carmen" (1922-1987), oto (1923-1945) , ljubomir (1929-2007), mario (1933-1984), anton half-siblings by her mother's first marriage: miroslava "mica" vukelic (1907-1993) and josip vukelic (1913-2004). milka's two marriages → married ivan anton defranceski (1925-1995) - who spent part of the war as a sixteen-year-old labourer in a german power works. the arolsen cards → children ladislava "ada" (b. 1948, crikvenica), ivan anton (b. 1951, senj), robert "robbie" (b. 1953, senj) emigrated april 1975, to south africa from zimbabwe later married santou (shemtov) isaac codron (1913-1997), born on rhodes - c. 1973, south africa died 30 october 2001, johannesburg, aged 75 cause cancer of the rectum, spread to the liver the shape of the life she was born into a household of seven children in a town whose economy had already collapsed - the railway had bypassed senj half a century before she was born. her mother supervised women rolling cigarettes; her father went to sea. she was fifteen when the independent state of croatia was declared and the war reached the coast, and nineteen when it ended and her brother oto did not come home. her first two children were born in yugoslavia , at crikvenica and senj. then africa - and it is worth being exact about the order, because the record is: she was in zimbabwe first , and came south to south africa in april 1975 . she is described as having married codron around 1973 , which places that marriage in the rhodesian years, not the south african ones. family lore, recorded september 2026 twenty-two years this archive cannot account for the record has her at senj in april 1953 , when robert was born, and in south africa in april 1975 , arriving from zimbabwe. between those two dates there is nothing at all - twenty-two years, an emigration, and an entire country she is only known to have been in because of the words "from zimbabwe" on the later entry. three things are remembered in the family about that crossing. they are set down here as what is said , beside what the record holds, and the two do not entirely agree. "they went in 1948" family lore remembered as the year ivan and hedviga left. the record does not allow it. their second and third children were born at senj in december 1951 and april 1953 . the family was in croatia for at least five years after 1948. but 1948 is a real year in this family , and it may be what the memory is anchored to: ladislava "ada" was born at crikvenica on 5 march 1948 . a date attaching itself to the wrong event is the commonest thing in this archive - it is how a man came to be born after his own granddaughter . why they went family lore a post-war migration , for better and safer conditions. nothing in the record speaks to motive at all - not a single document here says why anyone left. what the record does supply is the setting: a town whose economy had collapsed seventy years earlier, a brother dead in 1945 with no grave, and a husband who had spent the war from the age of sixteen as a labourer in a german power works . she sang at the hotel therapia family lore remembered as a singer at the hotel therapia in crikvenica - her husband's home town, and where their first child was born in 1948. the tree records no occupation for her whatsoever. her entire event list is three lines: born, immigrated, died. set against her mother - entered nadglednica u tvornici duhana , a supervisor in the tobacco factory - and her grandmother, a nadnicarka , that silence is its own kind of record. this is the only thing anyone has ever said about what hedviga did. and the venue is checkable, which lore rarely is. the therapia opened in 1895 as the nadvojvoda josip - archduke joseph - with 120 beds, and was renamed hotel therapia in 1899 when a hydropathic institute was established inside it. with the miramare of 1906 it is the building that turned crikvenica from a village into an austro-hungarian health resort . a woman singing there was singing in the grandest room on that stretch of coast. "i believe it closed down" corrected it did not. the building stands and is still a hotel. it was bought in 2013 by the austrian hotelier wilfried holleis , renovated, and renamed kvarner palace - four stars, 92 rooms. what closed was the name , not the house. which means the room she is remembered singing in is still there and can be walked into , and that is a rarer thing than a document. why this is written down rather than checked. a migration leaves paper - a passenger list, a permit, a naturalisation file, a school enrolment for three children. none of it has been looked for , because until now this archive did not know there was a rhodesian decade to look in. what would find it → two dates that fall on the same day 30 october her husband ivan anton defranceski died at senj on 30 october 1995 . hedviga died at johannesburg on 30 october 2001 - six years later, to the day. this archive records the coincidence and claims nothing by it. both dates come from the family tree rather than from a certificate seen here, and a shared date is exactly the kind of detail that gets tidied into place by memory. two death certificates would settle it , and they are the first documents on the wanted list. open questions → recovered from myheritage, september 2026 six pictures none of these are in the gedcom - myheritage does not export media - so the first build of this archive had no face to put to any of it. they are 480-pixel renderings , not the originals; the cdn signs each url against its size, so a bigger one cannot simply be asked for. almost certainly hedviga , c. late 1960s - the best likeness in the set, and the same face as the 1980s group below. very likely ivan and hedviga with their children , c. 1953-54 - a man in a suit holding a baby in a bonnet, a girl in a bolero, a small child in a beret. the ages fit ladislava, ivan and the infant robert. captioned "granny heddies photos-25" . colour, c. 1980s, a television and a video recorder behind - this is africa, not senj. eleven people in a garden, c. 1950s. the two older women seated at the centre are in black - widows' mourning. nobody in it is identified. five people and a dog, c. late 1950s - a boy on a bicycle, a man in a singlet, a truck behind. unidentified. not a photograph. the sworn translation of her son's 1951 yugoslav birth extract - and the one document here that confirms her own birth from outside the family tree. read it → four of these five photographs are unidentified. the tree carries them as filenames - 1595624858.9990501 , 1134835622 - with no names, dates or places attached. anyone who can put a name to a face in them should say so; that is the single most useful thing that could happen to this page. what the tree carries on her her record cites two independent trees - the defranceski family site and the boras web site - which is corroboration between witnesses, not between documents. why that distinction is kept →

and the family's use of it stops around 1838. so the wall at 1717 is not an archival wall. it is where the reading stopped. going further needs someone who can work in latin parish hands , who knows that x spells z in the older entries, and who is willing to search a name five ways . one structural caution. before civil registration, a parish register is the only record - and a fire, a war or a damp cellar ends a line absolutely. the military frontier was fought over repeatedly. some of these lines will not be extendable at any price, and it is better to know that than to keep guessing.

q: the blazevic archive an evidence-first archive for the family of hedviga blazevic of senj. senj · smokvica krmpotska · otocac · krivi put · selce · karlobag one woman, four families, and the mountain they were planted on. an evidence-first archive for hedviga "seka" blazevic - born at senj in 1926, dead at johannesburg in 2001 - and for the blazevici, zubrinici, papici and prpici who made her. illustration, not a photograph: a generated image of the northern adriatic coast, standing for senj under the velebit. every document reproduced on this site is the real scan. why the distinction is laboured here → this archive begins with one woman - hedviga "seka" blazevic , born at senj on 3 august 1926 , married to ivan anton defranceski, and dead at johannesburg on 30 october 2001 - and works outward into the four families that made her: the blazevici of smokvica krmpotska, the zubrinici of otocac, the papici of senj and selce, and the prpici of krivi put. it reaches nine generations and 70 named ancestors , the earliest born about 1717 . everything here is either sourced, reasoned in the open, or labelled as something the family says and the record does not yet confirm. start with hedviga the spine, nine generations what is still unproven it is a public archive with one rule: living people are absent from this build - q: kalanj the best-placed family in this archive - 87% of its records name a place - and the one whose house has just been seen wh klenovica and povile kalanj the best-placed family in this archive - 87% of its records name a place - and the one whose house has just been seen whole for the first time. 215 published people 1734 earliest birth year 3 distinct spellings in the tree one house, under two names eighty-five published kalanji carry a klenovica or povile house number, and every one of those houses is entirely kalanj - not one is shared with another surname. the two largest looked separate and are not. petrus kalanj and magdalena butkovic's ten children are entered povile 22, klenovica 22, klenovica 22, povile 22 , then four at klenovica 22, then two more at povile 22. ivan and josipa alternate the same way across seven children; luka and kata across four. no household moves house nine times and alternates back. povile and klenovica are neighbouring settlements and the registers used the two names for one place. so house 22 holds 67 published people between 1840 and 1890 - the largest single household in the archive, ahead of smokvica 114 and krivi put 136 . the gazetteer → and the smaller numbers are zadrugas too if house 22 is the extended household, the small late numbers ought to be sons splitting off. two of them are not. klenovica 23 (1862-1893) holds the children of four different couples - mate and catharina pa…, josephus and catharina buneta, jandre and manda komadina, joso and manda komadina. klenovica 36 (1892-1894) holds the children of three - luka and kata miletic, joso and manda, franjo and tereza. that is the same signature this archive identified at smokvica 114 : several married couples entered against one number in the same years. so the zadruga is not a smokvica peculiarity or a bunjevac one - it is how klenovica was organised too. houses 37, 38 and 59 hold a single child each and are something else, probably transient. one puzzle sits inside it. luka kalanj and kata miletic have children at house 22, then at 36 in 1892, then at 37 in 1894 - and two of them are called marija . whether that is a family moving twice in two years, a renumbering, or two entries for one child is not answerable from this file. four boys called antonius petrus and magdalena's children include an antonius born in 1865, another in 1868, a third in 1868 and a fourth in 1872. that is not an error. it is a necronym - a dead child's name given to the next born - and it is why the duplicate check has to read two death years as proof of two people rather than evidence of one. how they reach this archive not, as this page used to say, by marrying into the blazevic line - that is one marriage, lovro kalanj and klara blazevic. the chain that actually carries the family runs through hedviga's husband . ana kalanj , born at klenovica n° 22 on 3 january 1864 and baptised three days later, married josip de franceschi ; their son ante, their grandson pepe. every published kalanj is connected to hedviga by ordinary links - 100% , which only one other family here can say. what that means → four siblings, found loose in a photo library the baptisms of ana (1894), franciska (1896), zora (1898) and ivan (1900) - four consecutive children of martin kalanj and marija pericic at novi vinodolski - were sitting unattached in the family's own photographs. all four match the tree to the day , and the register calls the father martin kalanj josipov , a patronymic that confirms the grandfather independently of the tree. zora's godparents in 1898 are entered josip i ana defrancesco - the child's aunt and uncle , which is how ana's own place in this family was confirmed from a direction nobody was looking in. they are not a klenovica family. they are brinje people. this page, and this whole archive, has treated the kalanji as belonging to klenovica - 119 of them are recorded there. their own baptismal entry says otherwise, and it took an american passenger manifest to make anyone read the line properly. at ana kalanj's baptism, klenovica n° 22, 3 january 1864 , her parents are entered as josephus kalanj et rosalia nata perkovic ejus uxor, brinjensis parochiae ruricolae - country people of the parish of brinje . brinje is inland , over the kapela, some forty kilometres from the sea. and the tree independently records rozalija perkovic as being of brinje. so the klenovica kalanji came down to the coast, and every search this archive has run has been on the coast. brinje does not appear in the gazetteer and not one page of its register has been opened. and three of our surnames meet there the emigration records closed the triangle. stipe kalanj , born 1885, sailed for new york in 1910 on la bretagne , gave his residence as brinje , left a wife kate behind, and was met at the dock by his cousin, juro boric . this tree holds a jure boric of brinje - whose daughter ana boric , born 12 february 1885 at brinje, married frane papic of senj , born 27 july 1873. papic is hedviga's mother's family. kalanj, perkovic and boric are all at brinje, and a boric of brinje married a papic of senj. that is not proof they are one kin-group, and it is not offered as one. it is the observation that the parish where three of this archive's nine surnames overlap is the single parish nobody has ever looked in. what has been searched → and a death that may not need explaining this page said, for most of a day, that martin kalanj died at trebinje on 5 august 1900 - in herzegovina, four hundred kilometres from home, seven months after his youngest child was baptised at novi vinodolski - and that nothing here explained it. that was too credulous. his birth carries a full citation: familysearch 3qsq-g99x-kw8j , image 17 of 342, hrvatski drzavni arhiv image group 005494765. his death carries none - the source is a family tree, and the place is the bare word trebinje with no country attached. and this tree moves lika villages into bosnia. michael "mate" zubrinic, born 1863 at prozor near otocac, is geocoded in the same export to prozor in the herzegovina-neretva canton - two hundred kilometres away, across a border, and now the fourth geocoding error recorded here. so the question is no longer why did he go to herzegovina . it is whether he ever did - and a death register at novi vinodolski or klenovica would answer it faster than any search in trebinje. q: karlobag a small town under the velebit where this family's mothers came from - and, since 14 september 2026, the only parish in three films, four books and a household census karlobag a small town under the velebit where this family's mothers came from - and, since 14 september 2026, the only parish in this archive whose films have been opened end to end and whose census has been read. four of hedviga's great-great-great-grandparents were born here: the pilipici , the urode , the smojveri and the gerkacsi . for weeks the parish table carried unknown in all three of its columns, and four walls on the chart said «ranges not checked» - which reads like a gap and was really an unopened door. the door was opened. all three films, image by image. the holdings line now reads: births 1691-1770, 1771-1804, 1804-1861 · marriages 1736-1804, 1804-1861 · deaths 1774-1804, 1804-1861 · and a church census (stanje dusa) what the parish actually holds film images what is on it births 1691-1770 · 1771-1804 327 two bound volumes, hda 426 and hda 427 births · deaths · marriages 1804-1861, with indexes -
