q: method every claim here carries a confidence. the point of saying so is that a reader can disagree with the reasoning instead o how to read anything on this site method every claim here carries a confidence. the point of saying so is that a reader can disagree with the reasoning instead of having to take the conclusion on trust. the five words all seven of these family archives grade a claim with the same five words, so a level means the same thing wherever you meet it. the word is always printed next to the colour, because a reader should never have to know the palette to know the confidence. documented a record was read, and it says this. the source is named. probable the evidence points one way and nothing found so far points the other. not proven. inferred reasoned from what is known - a gap of the right size, a name in the right place - rather than witnessed in a record. family told, remembered, or written on a family chart. kept, because discarding it would lose the lead; labelled, because it is not evidence. disputed two sources disagree and neither has been ruled out. both are shown. not claimed some pages carry this instead. it states the thing a reader is likely to assume - the connection that would be tidy, the identification that almost works - and says plainly that this archive does not assert it. an archive is judged as much by what it refuses to say as by what it says. the five labels documented a named source with a reference, and where possible the scan. the strongest things in this archive are the familysearch citations into the croatian parish registers - senj, krivi put, otocac, karlobag - which give an image group, a page and a date. inferred a reasoned conclusion from documented facts, with the reasoning written out so it can be overturned. that the family is bunjevac is an inference from place and surname, not a statement in any record. superseded asserted in the family record, and now displaced by a document that says otherwise. disputed asserted in the family record but unsupported, or contradicted, by what can be seen - like the join at generation three . family lore told, remembered, not corroborated. kept because it is precious; labelled because pretending otherwise is how family myths become family history. both accounts of oto's death sit here. the rule that governs the whole build living people are not here they are not hidden, not gated, not present in the output. the rule is applied once, in classify_living() , at the boundary between the research data and the published site. because thousands of people in a tree this size carry no dates at all, judging each by their own record alone marks every one of them living - safe, but useless. so the build computes an upper bound on each person's birth year from their own events, their children's births, their marriages and their parents' bounds, and publishes somebody only when even the latest year they could have been born is more than a century ago. a recorded birth or christening → born in that year, exactly any recorded event in year e → born no later than e a child born in year c → born no later than c - 14 a marriage in year m → born no later than m - 14 a parent whose bound is p → born no later than p + 60 every step is a real bound, never a guess, and a recorded birth is never overridden by inference. on the current export that judges 2,034 of 15,643 people living. a living spouse, parent or child is not named on anybody else's page either. a removal request is honoured within days, without argument and without requiring a reason. this is stricter than its sister archives, and the difference is deliberate. the defranceschi archive publishes living people by name only - no dates, no places, no photographs , and the falco archive moved to the same rule in september 2026, naming 104 of them. this archive names none of its 2,034 . two reasons, and only one of them is principle. the scale is different - 2,034 living people against falco's 104 - and a rule that is comfortable for a hundred relatives is a different proposition for two thousand. and this archive is about one woman who died in 2001 : almost nothing it argues depends on anybody alive. where a living person is the only link in a chain, the page says "living, withheld" and the chain is shown broken rather than quietly completed. it is a divergence, not an oversight , and it is written here so that a reader moving between the family sites is not left wondering which rule is in force. an online family tree is a witness, not a source the spine here is a myheritage tree of 15,643 people . most "sources" attached to people in it are other trees - geni world family tree , boras web site , grlica web site , janicic , marko karic rodoslov . when four trees agree, that is four witnesses who may all have copied one another; it is not four documents. so the register page marks only whether a person carries any source string at all, and every person page prints the strings verbatim so a reader can see what kind of thing is being relied on. where a citation points at a parish register image , that is the one worth going to. sources → two things this archive does to the data, and admits to it folds spellings zubrinic, zubrinic, zubrinich, xubrinich and xubrinic are counted as one name ; so are prpic and perpic. without that, the family fragments into eight small families that appear unrelated. the folding is done in one function so it can be inspected and argued with. why the spellings differ → it drops the working scaffolding the tree contains sorting stubs - "senj - unknown to be sorted papic" , "brothers [of stephanus] zubrinic" , "nn blazevic" . these are research notes, not people, and publishing them as ancestors would be a lie. they are filtered by name pattern at the build boundary. what is not committed the raw gedcom is not published - it contains every living person in full. it is kept out of any public copy of this repository and regenerated from a fresh myheritage export when needed.

q: milka hedviga's mother is the best-documented person in this archive: a birth entry, two marriage entries, a gravestone and a senj, 9 october 1886 - 7 september 1971 milka hedviga's mother is the best-documented person in this archive: a birth entry, two marriage entries, a gravestone and a factory. her life can be told almost entirely from records, and it is not the life the family tree describes. the tree carries milka lucia papic as the wife of ljubomir blazevic and the mother of seven. the registers carry a woman who was married twice , widowed at twenty-eight , and spent more than forty years in the same tobacco factory - going in as a floor worker and coming out supervising it. senj baptisms, page 122, entry 96 born 9 october 1886 senj, roman catholic baptisms, str. 122 , entry 96. her entry is the second from the bottom of the left-hand page. name milka lucia - zakonita , legitimate born / baptised 9 october 1886 , baptised 17 october father josip papic , trhonosa - a load-carrier mother tonka rod. prpic godparents josip glavicic , also a trhonosa , and ivka filipovic baptised by the chaplain ( kapelan ) at senj later annotation the margin was written up again when she died - the register records the death entry and the date 7.9.1971 , endorsed at senj 30.9.1971 . a small correction. the family tree gives her baptism as 19 october . the register says 17 . the archive follows the register. both her father and her godfather are trhonose - men who carried other people's goods on their backs for a fee. that is not a coincidence; it is a social world. in a port town whose port had died, the porters knew the porters . senj marriages, page 294, entry 30 first marriage, 4 november 1907 aged twenty-one, she married zvonimir m. vukelic - and nothing in the family tree's account of her had ever mentioned it. senj marriages, page 294, entry 30, boxed in red on the scan as held in the tree. date 4 studenoga (november) 1907 , senj groom zvonimir m. vukelic , gostionicarski pomocnik - innkeeper's assistant . born 13 january 1883 . bachelor. bride milka papic , radnica u tvornici duhana - a worker in the tobacco factory. born 9 october 1886. unmarried. his parents vukelic pl. petar , gostionicar - innkeeper - and † vjekoslava , surname read as putnic (possibly putinic - not settled) . the dagger stands before vjekoslava, not before petar: it is the mother who was dead in 1907. her parents joso papic, gostionicar and tonka rod. prpic witnesses koloman pl. vukelic , mestar u tvornici duhana - q: the names blazevic is the seventeenth commonest surname in croatia. zubrinic is held by about three hundred people on earth. both four surnames, one of them almost extinct the names blazevic is the seventeenth commonest surname in croatia. zubrinic is held by about three hundred people on earth. both are in this family, and the rare one is the one that travels. what they mean blazevic - "son of blaz" a patronymic from the given name blaz , the croatian form of blasius / blaise, itself from latin blaesus , "lisping" or "stammering". the suffix -evic / -ic is the ordinary south slavic "child of". it is the 17th most frequent surname in croatia . its densest counties are split-dalmatia, virovitica-podravina and osijek-baranja - not lika-senj. our blazevici sit outside the name's main clusters, which is a caution: sharing this surname with someone is nearly meaningless as evidence. zubrinic - the rare one about 312 bearers worldwide , of whom 292 are in croatia at a density of 1:14,482. within croatia its two great concentrations are the city of zagreb (28%) and lika-senj county (25%) - and lika-senj is where tereza and her forebears at otocac are from. a name this rare behaves in the opposite way to blazevic: two zubrinici in the otocac registers are probably related. that makes it the most useful surname in this archive. papic - "son of the priest", or of papa from pop / papa - priest. the tree itself preserves the alternate form: seventy-nine of its papici are written papic (papa) , and the direct ancestor is recorded as "georgius juraj (joannis) papa 'jure' antic papic" - carrying antic and papic at once. the family was changing its name in the record, in front of us. prpic - and perpic a hypocoristic patronymic, from a short form of a given name. in this tree it is written prpic 83 times, perpic 19, perpic 16, prpic 8 - and one record hedges openly as "papic or perpic" . antonija herself is entered as "perpic / prpic" . prpic concentrates in zagreb (27%), primorje-gorski kotar (17%) and lika-senj (13%) - again the family's own ground. the most important thing on this page x wrote the sound z the zubrinic name appears in this tree in eight different spellings , and they are not errors. they are three successive orthographies for one unchanged spoken name. xubrinich the venetian-italian convention used along this coast, in which x stood for the sound written z in modern croatian, and -ch for -c . latin-language parish registers in habsburg croatia use it constantly. zubrinich the german-latin compromise of the imperial administration: the diacritic dropped because the clerk's alphabet had no way to write it, the -ich ending kept. zubrinic modern croatian , after gaj's diacritical reform of the 1830s made z and c standard. this is the form the family uses today. the direct ancestors are entered under both at once - nicolaus "nikola" zubrinic (xubrinic) , born at otocac on 24 january 1834, and his father michael "mate" zubrinic / zubrinic / xubrinich , born 1811. whoever built this tree was reading across all three systems, which is the right instinct. the practical consequence. searching croatian records for zubrinic alone will miss most of the family before about 1850. the name has to be searched as xubrinich , zubrinich , xubrinic and zubrinic as well - and this archive's own tooling folds all of them to one key before it counts anything. the surname is only half the problem the given names change language too these registers were kept in latin , and then in croatian . the same man is joannes in the book that baptised him and ivan in the one that married him - and a fair number of entries decline him into joannem or joannis , because a priest writing baptizavi josephum is writing the accusative, not the name. so the archive's own register was splitting people from themselves . a reader searching ivan was shown 42 of them and not the other 46 . of 29 canonical given names in ante and antonija . they are not the same name , and this archive first merged them by mistake - which would have told a reader that fourteen franciskas were franjos. they are split by sex, and counted separately. a consequence worth its own section forty people in this archive are named after a case ending these registers are narrative latin , not forms. a priest writes baptizavi josephum - "i baptised josephus" - and filius josephi - "son of josephus". those endings are grammar . transcribed literally into a family tree, they become names, and the tree acquires a man called josephum who endings were one person working through a run of selce and vinodol entries - a modern transcriber lifting the word after baptizavi . three scans read since then show that is wrong. the priests wrote the oblique forms themselves. register what the page actually says form vrbnik, 14 march 1806 michael kombol …patre joanne, matre marthae antich papa, nomine josephum accusative karlobag, august 1789 andreas baglietich mariam natam pridie ex michaele et lucia gergacs accusative karlobag, april 1777 joannes a. ivankovich cui impositum est nomen joannis georgij genitive two parishes, three priests, three decades apart. in the 1806 book every child on the page is named in the accusative - mariam, joannem, matthaeam, magdalenam, vincentium, nicolaum. that is not a slip anyone made; it is how the sentence works. baptizavi infantem … nomine josephum - the child is the grammatical object of the verb, so the child's name takes the object's ending. and karlobag settles it from a single hand. one priest, joannes antonius ivankovich , writing in the same book four years apart: 1777 cui impositum est nomen joannis georgij genitive 1781 cui impositum est nomen oliva maria nominative the same formula, the same parish, the same man - and a different case each time. a third karlobag priest, michael martinaz, writes nomen caetani antonij in 1779. it is not a rule and it is not an error: it is scribal caprice , and a tree that copies the word faithfully inherits whichever case the priest happened to use that morning. which makes the ending useful. if the case is the register's own grammar rather than an error, it records how that person appeared in the entry they were found in : accusative - josephum , mariam - they were the one being baptised. the entry is their own . genitive or dative - joannis , pauli , simoni - they were named as somebody's parent. the entry belongs to their child , and they appear only in passing. so the six ancestors carrying a genitive are people this archive has never yet seen a record of - only records that mention them. that is a reading list, not a defect. what would close them → and the registers underline the by-names. the 1806 vrbnik scribe rules a line under a second name after the surname - antich papa , loncsarich franich , antich dudin , pobor rataj . these are nadimci , house by-names that tell one household from another where a whole village shares a surname - the same problem the house numbers solve. it also puts a documented papa beside the 79 people this tree writes papic (papa) , and leaves an open question: whether that is the by-name of an antic household rather than a surname in its own right. the papic line → nothing has been renamed. the tree is the authority on what the tree says, and this archive's job is to note where what it says is a grammatical artefact rather than to quietly correct it - the person pages carry the note, and the search folds the forms together so that josephum and josip find each other. read this before you search the name what the surname-origin websites say about zubrinic is invented because zubrinic is rare, it is exactly the kind of name that the automated "meaning and origin of your surname" sites fill in with confident fiction. one of them, consulted for this archive, produced the following - and it is worth setting out, because somebody researching this family will find it. "a croatian ban" it names "petar zubrinic, an 18th-century croatian ban" . the bans of croatia in that century were palffy, draskovic, eszterhazy, branyng, batthyany, nadasdy, esterhazy, balassa and erdody . there was no ban zubrinic. the claim is fabricated. two etymologies the same site derives the name from zubor , "babble" - a talkative man - and from zubr / zubr , the aurochs . these are unrelated words. it concedes the second is " nije potvrdeno ", unconfirmed, having just asserted the first. the wrong region it states the name "originates from dalmatia and is most prevalent there today". the distribution figures below put 25% of croatian bearers in lika-senj and 28% in the city of zagreb - the usual modern drift to a capital - and dalmatia nowhere . this family's own records run through otocac , in lika, for two centuries. noble status asserted for the 17th century, with no document, by a source that has already invented a viceroy. what can honestly be said is small. the name is a standard -ic patronymic built on a stem zubr- ; which personal name or nickname stands behind that stem is a question for croatian onomastic scholarship, and this archive has not found an authority that answers it. everything else on this page is counted, not guessed. method → the general lesson is worth more than the particular one. a surname-origin website that cites nothing is not a weak source; it is not a source. the safe test is the one applied here: take its single most checkable factual claim - a named person holding a named office in a named century - and check it. and then the name emigrates when the family leaves, the spelling forks permanently - and the two forks can be counted separately. form bearers where they are zubrinic - the homeland form 312 croatia 292, serbia 14, montenegro 6. 100% in europe. zubrinic - the diaspora form 69 argentina 29, canada 16, united states 8, south africa 7 , netherlands 5. none in croatia at all. the two lists do not overlap by a single country. the diacritics are not decoration; they are a border. and the seven in south africa are on the same continent this family's own line ended up on. the australian branch spells it zubrinich → distribution, as counted name worldwide density principal countries blazevic 11,163 1:652,830 croatia 7,216 (1:586) · bosnia 3,058 · serbia 492 papic 6,014 1:1,211,764 serbia 2,894 · croatia 1,611 · bosnia 1,165 prpic 1,218 1:5,983,207 croatia 1,071 (1:3,948) · serbia 75 · bosnia 55 zubrinic 312 1:23,357,519 croatia 292 (1:14,482) · serbia 14 · montenegro 6 figures from forebears, which builds on national statistical and electoral registers. they are good for orders of magnitude and for relative density; q: open questions written down so they can be worked on, and so no reader mistakes a gap for a fact. each one says what would actually clo 19 open · 9 answered open questions written down so they can be worked on, and so no reader mistakes a gap for a fact. each one says what would actually close it. the most valuable thing anyone can send this archive is a correction . the second most valuable is a document that closes one of these. answered - kept so the change is visible 1. who were ljubomir's parents? - answered this was the archive's central doubt: the join at generation three rested on a man with no document. the senj marriage register of 8 december 1920 names the groom's parents outright - juraj blazevic and tereza r. zubrinic - and confirms ljubomir's birth as 1 march 1892. it was attached in the family tree the whole time and absent from the gedcom export. what would settle it: nothing further. what replaces it is question 1b. substantive 1b. who was juraj blazevic's father? - a house number, and a second witness four more registers were read in september 2026 and the man is no longer a bare name. he has an occupation and a house. his son marijan's baptism, 12 april 1895 , enters him as "jurko blazevic i tereza rod. zubrinic, selj. " - peasant - living at smokvica kbr. 114 . that house is a zadruga, not a household - this archive's own correction. toma and terezija pecanic are recorded at smokvica 114 in 1882 and 1884 , and toma was born at br. 114 in 1838. but a control document - the 1890 baptism of frane blazevic - puts pavao blazevic, son of luka , at smokvica 114 as well. luka and toma's father anton are both sons of ilija , so pavao and toma are first cousins, and the number covers an extended-family compound . it places juraj in ilija's kin-group; it cannot name his father. the zadruga → and a second register names the couple. anka blazevic's marriage to pavao kosina on 20 november 1919 gives her parents as juraj blazevic i tereza r. zubrinic - independently of the 1920 entry for their son ljubomir. and the house is now written out in full. antonija "tonka" blazevic's marriage to ginro babic on 1 december 1912 enters her parents as "††toma i tereza blazevic, poljodjelci iz sela smokvica kbr. 114 " - not a number in a baptismal margin but the household stated in plain croatian, both of them marked dead. that is a fourth independent document for house 114 and the first to name toma and tereza together with the number. it hardens the household the whole argument stands on; it still does not name juraj's father. what would settle it: and the godparents close the circle. the tree gives juraj two younger siblings, marija (b. 1880) and ivan (b. 1882) - children of toma at house 114. the godparents at marijan's 1895 baptism are entered as "ive blazevic, sin tomin " and "marija blazevic, cer tomina " : the son and the daughter of a toma, of the right names and the right ages, standing for the child of the man who lives in toma's house. with the house number demoted to a kin-group, the godparents carry the weight - and they carry it well. godparents are chosen , and a man's own brother and sister are the classic choice. september 2026 - and the patronymic turns out to be deliberate. reading the 1888 baptism of pavao's daughter terezija, also at smokvica 114, gives a godfather called ivo blazevic sin matin - son of mate . so two different men named ivo blazevic stood godfather at this one house within seven years , told apart only by their fathers' names. that is why the priest bothered with a patronymic at all: there were several ivo blazevici about, and "sin tomin" in 1895 is a distinction he chose to draw, not a formula. it also shows the compound from the outside - one house number holding toma's children, pavao's children, jurko's children, an ivo son of toma and an ivo son of mate. september 2026 - and the godparent column says it plainly. four baptisms at smokvica 114 have now been read, and the godparents are drawn from two distinct blazevic sibling-sets : 1888 ivo blazevic sin matin · anica tomljanovic 1894 sime pecanic · mara blazevic matina 1895 ive blazevic sin tomin · marija blazevic cer tomina 1896 nikola blazevic · ana krpan kci ilijina mate's children and toma's children, both standing at the same house, plus a pecanic - toma's wife's family. that is what a zadruga looks like from the godparent column : one number, several fathers, and the children of one brother standing for the children of another. it still does not name jurko's father; it does make the compound something you can see rather than infer. it is still not the sentence that says so. what would give it: jurko's own baptism in the sv. jakov krmpote register, or his marriage to tereza zubrinic before 1892. two of his children, marijan (1895) and ruza (1897) , have no marriage recorded anywhere - and every marriage entry re-names the parents, so those are two more chances at the same answer. answered - kept so the change is visible 1c. who was milka's first husband? - answered zvonimir m. vukelic , gostionicarski pomocnik - innkeeper's assistant - born 13 january 1883, married at senj on 4 november 1907 (marriages p.294 no.30 - read at full resolution 13 september 2026, image 299 of the film). he died in 1915 , aged thirty-two, leaving milka a widow at twenty-eight. their children miroslava "mica" vukelic (1907-1993) and josip vukelic (1913-2004) are hedviga's half-sister and half-brother - and were in the tree all along. milka's life → what would settle it: nothing further on identity. what remains is 1d. worth doing 1d. how did zvonimir vukelic die in 1915? - and a correction this archive proposed the austro-hungarian casualty lists, reasoning that he was thirty-two in the second year of the war. that reasoning was probably wrong. the tree places his death at senj , in his own town, and gives his occupation as gostionicar, bankar - innkeeper and banker , a considerable rise from the gostionicarski pomocnik who married milka in 1907. a man who dies at home, in a settled trade, is not a verlustliste entry. his baptism has since been read: born 13 january 1883 at senj, baptised 25 february, son of petar pl. vukelic - plemeniti , noble - and lojza. milka married into a titled family and was widowed out of it at twenty-eight. what would settle it: and a third occupation, from a third document. on 16 august 1914 he stands witness at the wedding of milka's sister franjka, entered as "zvonko m. vukelic, pivar " - brewer. the trajectory now reads gostionicarski pomocnik (1907) → pivar (1914) → gostionicar, bankar (at death). it is also the first document found that places him inside this family other than his own marriage entry. the senj death register for 1915 , and nothing else. the casualty lists are behind a subscription for uncommon surnames and are, on this evidence, the wrong book. worth doing 1e. which came first - the wedding or the child? milka and zvonimir married on 4 november 1907 by episcopal dispensation, with the banns read once on 3 november rather than three times. their daughter miroslava was born in 1907 . a dispensation, a one-day wedding and a child in the same year make a familiar shape - but the register does not date the birth, and this archive does not claim to know. weakened 13 september 2026. the senj marriage of martin kosina and angjelika boras, 12 january 1888 , carries the same shape: dispensed by the senj ordinariate on 7 january, banns read once only on the 8th, married on the 12th. he was 47 and she 30 , and there is no suggestion of anything in it. a single dispensation in this diocese looks like ordinary administrative practice, not evidence - so this question rests on the birth date alone, and that is exactly what is missing. what would settle it: miroslava vukelic's baptismal entry, senj 1907 , which gives the day. critical - the spine depends on it 2. how did oto blazevic die? two accounts in the same note, from two named relatives: a snakebite , and killed in the war in slavonia with no known grave . a photograph of the family grave now corroborates the second witness in its checkable parts - oto's name is on the stone, and leo and katica were added later exactly as she described. it still does not establish the cause . the full page → what would settle it: a search of the yugoslav war victims register ( popis zrtava rata ) and croatian state archives military death records for oto blazevic, b. 1923, senj . an entry - or a confirmed absence - settles it. substantive 3. when did santou codron leave rhodes? born on rhodes in 1913 ; alive in south africa to marry hedviga about 1973 . the island's jewish community was deported on 23 july 1944 and roughly 150 of 1,615 survived. whether he left before the war - as ~2,000 rhodes jews did, for the congo and rhodesia - or survived the deportation is not known here , and the difference is enormous. the full page → what would settle it: south african immigration and naturalisation papers giving arrival year and last residence; the rhodes jewish museum community registers and yad vashem deportation lists, searched for codron. critical - the spine depends on it 4. is the port pirie branch the same zubrinic family? now traceable three generations back from the emigrant: ivan zubrinic (1860-1930) → his father joannes, b. 19 june 1837, forest ranger → elias "ilija" (1806-1845) → casparus (1767-1829) . and there it stops: in the tree, casparus's parent is a node literally named "brothers of casparus (it seems) zubrinic" - a researcher's guess written into the structure. nothing joins the two lines - and as of 13 september 2026 it is possible to say exactly what the apparent join is made of. walk casparus upward and the chain reads: casparus 1767 → "brothers of casparus (it seems)" → "c zubrinic xubrinich zubrinic" → "zubrinic zubrinix xubrinic zubrinic otocac" . the second is a researcher's note. the third is an alphabet - one of eighteen nodes whose entire given name is a single letter, holding everyone whose name starts with it. ninety-two people are attached that way. walk toma upward and he stops at a bare node called zubrinic after one step. so the two lines meet in a filing system and nowhere else. but they are born a year apart in one small village. casparus 14 january 1767; toma 1768, at sumecica 2 - and the 1834 frontier baptism this archive has read is at sumecica 24 . a surname held by ~312 people on earth, two men born a year apart in the same hamlet. the frontier → what would settle it: the 1760s baptisms do not exist in any collection reachable from here - checked 13 september 2026. familysearch's otocac holdings begin in 1834 . this question's stated next step has been unavailable the whole time, and better image access does not change that. but the same parish holds a better document, and this archive had never looked at it. church census (stanje dusa) 1710-1846 - a status animarum , filmed at the croatian state archives as otocac knj. 1 , 384 images. it is not a register of events but a standing list of households , and its columns are the ones this question actually needs: pagus the village domus the house number nomina familiae every member, relationship spelled out dies/mensis/annus a birth date for each a baptism register would give two fathers' names. this book would give the house - and for a question about whether two men born a year apart in one hamlet belong to one zadruga , the house is the better answer. it covers 1767 and 1768. what it will cost. it is not in familysearch's full-text index - tested, the query returns nothing - and there is no index at the front of the book. the pagus is written sideways in the gutter and vanishes into the binding shadow on many frames, so it cannot even be navigated by village reliably. that means about 110 openings read one at a time , looking for zubrinic in the name column and sumecica in the margin. a sitting, not a lookup - but a sitting that can actually be taken. notes/otocac-status-animarum.md and a warning about the other book on the same film. the otocac marriage register 1859-1872 was opened the same day and read: images 129-147, latin, ruled, pag. 10 = 1862 , pag. 18 = 1865 . it has no parents column. it gives a name, a trade, a village, a house number, an age and whether the person was single - and never a father. so it cannot push any line upward, and no plan should assume it will. one entry was read in full: 25 september 1859, nicolaus zubrinic, vicedecu… - a military frontier rank - of prozor, aged 24, marrying anna dujmovic of prozor, aged 18 , with lucas zubrinic among the witnesses. aged 24 in 1859 means born about 1834-35, and ahnentafel 10 is a nicolaus zubrinic born 1834 . it is deliberately not claimed as his. the tree gives ahn 10's wife as ana maric , not dujmovic; the surname is thick on the ground in this parish; and this archive has already once announced a direct ancestor as a duplicate on exactly this kind of name-and-year coincidence. what would settle it is tereza zubrinic's baptism, 29 november 1867 at otocac - and otocac baptisms stop at 1858 , nine years short. 14 september 2026 - the census was read, and it does not hold this family. the pagus margin turned out to be perfectly legible: the village is written bottom-to-top in the gutter, so the earlier sitting's rotation rendered it upside down and it read as noise. rotated the other way, twenty-two openings gave the village order of the whole book - ottosaz · luka · dubrava · novoselia · lieska · kostelievo selo · obilje · beljue · shumechicza · luka · extinctae - and put sumecica at images 102-106. five openings, not a hundred and ten. all five were read. the households are dasovic (domus 9), stabincic (10), orehovic (4) , a paulus household, a household of andreas and stephanus, janezic, ollar, kovacic, orehovacki . there is no zubrinic at sumecica in this book, and no domus 2 and no domus 24. the extinctae section was read too; the ruled census stops about image 112 and what follows has no pagus column at all. the likeliest reading is that the sumeci 

s: Hedviga's brother died at twenty-two in the last year of the war. The family preserves two accounts of how, they cannot
q: the brother hedviga's brother died at twenty-two in the last year of the war. the family preserves two accounts of how, they cannot oto blazevic, 1923-1945 the brother hedviga's brother died at twenty-two in the last year of the war. the family preserves two accounts of how, they cannot both be true, and there is no grave to ask. this page exists because the record contains a contradiction that has been kept rather than tidied away . both accounts are written into the same note on oto's entry, attributed to two different people, and this archive reproduces them exactly as they stand. the first account bitten by snake - attributed in the tree to ivan defranceski ivan anton defranceski (1925-1995) was hedviga's husband and oto's brother-in-law - two years younger than oto, and alive in the same town at the time. the velebit has the horned viper , vipera ammodytes , europe's most dangerous snake, and a shepherd or a labourer on that mountain was genuinely at risk. the second account the late otto blazevic was the brother of ljuba, leo, aunt karma, aunt seka … he died in the war somewhere in slavonia , his grave is unknown, so they put his name in his grandmother's and grandfather's grave - and now leo is there, and katica. - attributed in the tree to nives blazevic this one names his siblings correctly, including "aunt seka" - hedviga's own nickname - which is a good sign that the speaker knew the family well. what the second account fits the war in slavonia in 1945 is not a vague setting. it is one of the best-documented killing grounds of the european war's last months. the syrmian front ran from 21 october 1944 to 12 april 1945 across syrmia, slavonia and baranja. the yugoslav partisans lost more than 13,500 killed covering roughly 140 kilometres between belgrade and vinkovci over nearly six months of winter fighting. when the front broke on 12 april, the 1st and 3rd armies advanced west through slavonia . he had already seen the war close up. he was twenty when german aircraft destroyed about half of senj on 7-8 october 1943 , killing thirty of the town's residents - among them, on the second day, his uncle by marriage pavao kosina . a man born in 1923 was twenty-one or twenty-two in that campaign - precisely the cohort mobilised into it, much of it from newly-liberated croatia with minimal training. and an unknown grave is the ordinary outcome, not the strange one: thousands of those dead were buried where they fell. the detail that rings true. that the family cut his name into his grandparents' stone because there was no body is a specific, unglamorous, expensive act. people do it when someone does not come back from somewhere far away. it is much harder to explain if he died of a snakebite on the hill above the town. new evidence, september 2026 the grave says she was right about the grave a photograph of the blazevic plot at senj - recovered from the myheritage media library, where it had been sitting untouched - can be checked against nives blazevic's account line by line. it matches. ljubomir blazevic ✳1891 †1966 · milka blazevic rod. papic ✳1886 †1971 · oto blazevic ✳1923 †1945 · mario blazevic ✳1933 †1984 - and, on a later plaque, kata ✳1924 †2007 and leo ✳1920 †2008. she said "they put his name in … [the] grave" the stone oto blazevic ✳ 1923 † 1945 is cut into it, between his mother and his brother mario. she said "and now leo is there, and katica " the stone a separate, later, black plaque below reads leo ✳ 1920 † 2008 and kata ✳ 1924 † 2007 - katica. she said "his grandmother's and grandfather's grave" the stone the names are oto's parents . but nives blazevic was born in 1953 - ljubomir and milka were her grandparents. she is describing the grave from where she stands in the family, which is what people do. what this does and does not settle. it does not show that oto died in slavonia. it shows that the witness who said so knew this grave in exact detail , including two burials added more than sixty years after his death - and that the family commemorated him on a stone rather than at a grave of his own, which is what you do for a man who does not come back. the snakebite account now sits second. how this archive leaves it documented born 1923, senj. died 1945, with the death place entered in the tree as senj . son of ljubomir blazevic and milka papic; brother of leo, karmela, hedviga, ljubomir, mario and anton. family lore, first snakebite. attributed to ivan defranceski, who was there. family lore, second killed in the war in slavonia, no known grave, name added to his grandparents' plot. attributed to nives blazevic. corroborated nives's account, in its checkable parts: his name on the family stone, and leo and katica added to it later. the grave → contradiction still unresolved as to cause. the tree's own death place of senj agrees with neither account cleanly - it contradicts slavonia outright, and it is also exactly what a family would enter when the real place was unknown. what would settle it. the croatian state archives hold second world war military and civil death records, and the yugoslav war victims register ( popis zrtava rata ) is searchable by name and birth year. a single entry for oto blazevic, b. 1923, senj would end the question in either direction. nobody has yet looked. open questions → both accounts are kept because pretending otherwise is how family myths become family history - and because one of these two people was right. method →

q: papic porters, carriers and an innkeeper on the senj waterfront - and, one generation on, a woman supervising the floor of the senj and selce papic porters, carriers and an innkeeper on the senj waterfront - and, one generation on, a woman supervising the floor of the town's cigarette factory. 116 published people 1742 earliest birth year 4 distinct spellings in the tree one change in four documents the tree lists josip "joso" papic's occupations as trhonosa, bremenar, gostionicar - load-carrier, porter, innkeeper - as though they were three trades in a row. four parish registers give him four words, and only one of them is a change. at his own wedding in 1885 he is a bremenar ; at his daughter milka's baptism in 1886 , a trhonosa ; at his daughter anica's in 1888 , a tezak . those are not three trades - they are three words a priest reached for to mean a man who works with his body : burden-carrier, load-carrier, labourer. then at milka's wedding in 1907 he is a gostionicar . that is the change. he owns the inn. milka → the tobacco factory his daughter milka lucia papic (1886-1971) - hedviga's mother - was supervisor of workers at the cigarette factory in senj, an address the tree records as ul. stjepana radica 4 , "now a textile factory". she was baptised at senj on 19 october 1886 , ten days after her birth, with josip glavicic and ivka filipovic as godparents - one of the best-cited entries in this archive. a name changing in front of us the selce line is entered as "georgius juraj (joannis) papa 'jure' antic papic " - carrying antic and papic at once - and seventy-nine people in this tree are written papic (papa) . the register settles that this is a real alternation and not a transcriber's slip: in the 1885 marriage entry the groom is josip papic and his father, on the very same line, is juraj papa . and the doubling is old: the 1806 baptismal entry for josephum at vinodol enters his mother as "matre marthe antich papa " - both names on one line, eighty years before the tree's papic (papa) . his godfather is the village judge , judice mathia jellichich - of the family he would marry into. whether antic and papic were ever two families is now the open question. open questions → why the papici have no house number the blazevici can be traced through a single house number because the village registers of krmpote and krivi put record every child against one - smokvica 114 , krivi put 136 . the senj register does not. under mjesto obitavanja i kucni broj - place of residence and house number - the papic entries say simply "senj" , and nothing else. that is a difference between a town and a village, not between two families. it also means the zadruga that is visible at smokvica would be invisible here even if it existed , and no amount of reading senj baptisms will show it. the other half of this family hedviga's descent is not all peasants, and the other half arrives through this family. josip papic's mother was matija pilipic , and through her the line runs into karlobag , a free royal city on the coast under the velebit, and the register there speaks a different language about them: dominus at the 1768 baptism of josephus pilipic; negotiator - merchant - when he is named as deceased in 1838; and godparents who are franciscus de justiniani , a venetian patrician name, and, in 1777, pro-colonel joannes hallinich de zirfeld with the wife of centurion daniel de kalbenaeck . a colonel and a captain's wife stood for an uroda child; a giustiniani for a pilipic. that is not the world of smokvica 114 , and the two meet in one woman four generations later. the marriage, 3 february 1885 senj marriages p.192, entry 5. josip papic , bremenar , of senj, aged 27 , bachelor, married antonia perpic of krivi put , resident at senj, aged 26 , spinster. banns published; married by the chaplain mirko babic . his parents: juraj papa, tezak - a farm labourer - and matia rod. pilipic . hers: ivan perpic, seljak - peasant - and luca rod. perpic , which supplies a maiden name the tree did not carry: antonija's mother was herself a perpic . the witnesses are franjo and toma perpic , both peasants - the bride's s: Seven places and four kinds of paper. Each one is here because a specific claim on this site would move if somebody stoo
q: photograph these seven places and four kinds of paper. each one is here because a specific claim on this site would move if somebody stoo for whoever is next in croatia photograph these seven places and four kinds of paper. each one is here because a specific claim on this site would move if somebody stood in front of it with a phone - not because it would be nice to have. this archive has been built from a family tree, a media library and about thirty pages of parish register read on a screen. nobody involved in it has stood in any of these places. a phone is enough for all of it; none of this needs an appointment, and most of it needs no permission. photograph the whole thing and then the detail. a stone shot only close up cannot be placed in its row; a stone shot only wide cannot be read. and photograph the ones that look like nothing - a wrong house number is worth knowing too. go here first senj - the cemetery at sv. vid the blazevic grave: ljubomir 1892-1966, milka 1886-1971, oto 1923-1945, mario 1933-1984. photograph the whole stone and each line close. tereza zubrinic's stone, 1867-1931, restored by the kosina family in 1991, with the wooden cross for vlc. antun kosina 1921-2003 standing against it. pavao and anka kosina's grave - his stone reads nevina zrtva zracnog napadaja na senj, an innocent victim of the air raid. why: toma blazevic was buried here on 28 july 1907 and stanko papic on 4 june 1903. neither grave has been looked for. a cemetery register or a surviving stone would place them. smokvica krmpotska - house 114 the house itself, if it still stands, and the number if it is still on it. the neighbouring numbers, 112 and 116, so the run can be placed on the ground. anything carved or dated on the building. why: six documented years - 1838, 1882, 1884, 1888, 1890, 1895 - hold toma's children, pavao's children, jurko's children and two different men called ivo blazevic. it is the zadruga the whole of question 1b turns on, and nobody in this archive has seen it. klenovica and povile - house 22 the house, if it stands, and the number on it - in both villages, because they may be the same building. whether klenovica 22 and povile 22 are one house, two houses, or one house the registers gave two village names. the kalanj graves in the klenovica cemetery beyond the one already photographed (lovro 1906-1965, ana 1919-1971, ivan 1942-1996, marijan 1944-2009). why: sixty-seven published people are entered at house 22 between 1840 and 1890 - the largest single household in this archive, ahead of smokvica 114 and krivi put 136. eleven couples have children recorded under both village names, which is why it is thought to be one house. nobody has stood in front of it. krivi put - house 136 the house, and 113 and 129 if the numbers survive. the church of the parish, and any war memorial. why: antonija perpic was born at 136 in 1859 into a household the register calls confiniarii. three prpic house numbers are known and none has been seen. when you are passing crikvenica - the hotel therapia the building, now the kvarner palace - the facade and, if they will let you in, the room that was the dining hall. any historic photograph the hotel keeps of its own interwar years. why: hedviga is remembered singing here. it is the only thing anyone has ever said about what she did, and the building is still standing - bought in 2013 and renamed. a photograph would turn a sentence of lore into something you can look at. senj - the tobacco factory the building on ul. stjepana radica 4, now a textile works. any plaque, date stone or surviving signage. why: milka supervised women rolling cigarettes here and antonija blazevic held the same grade. across ten register pages between 1909 and 1919, most young women marrying in senj worked in it. if you get that far otocac and sumecica sumecica house 24, if the numbering survives. the parish church at otocac. prozor houses 50 and 245. why: the 1834 baptism puts a confiniarius household at sumecica 24. the zubrinici held five frontier offices out of these villages. karlobag the parish church. anything marking the town as a free royal city - the registers call it hujus civitatis. why: four generations of pilipici, urodas, smojvers and gerkacs, with a giustiniani standing godfather and a baron von holstein on the same page. the most socially distinct part of this descent. and anything on paper what why it matters here anything written on the back of a photograph studio stamps date and place a picture better than anything else here. fifteen photographs on /faces have no caption but a camera filename. letters, in any language nothing in this archive is in the family's own words. not one letter. identity papers, passports, work books a yugoslav passport application would date the emigration that question 1f cannot. funeral cards and death notices they carry the date, the parish and often the surviving relatives, all three. if you are holding a photograph and cannot say who is in it, that is worth as much - the contact sheet is fifteen pictures this archive cannot vouch for, and one conversation would close most of it.

s: With one exception, every place in this archive before 1884 lies within a day's walk of the Velebit — and the exception
q: places with one exception, every place in this archive before 1884 lies within a day's walk of the velebit - and the exception a hundred kilometres of coast, and then two other continents places with one exception, every place in this archive before 1884 lies within a day's walk of the velebit - and the exception is the whole point. one of the places below has never been searched at all, and it is where a whole family came from. senj the port town. birthplace of hedviga, milka and josip papic; deathplace of toma blazevic, ljubomir, milka and antonija. everything converges here. smokvica krmpotska the blazevic village in the vinodol hills, settled by bunjevci in the 17th century. house 114 is toma's. krivi put the prpic village on the senj mountain. house 136 produced 35 people in this tree. otocac the zubrinic town, in the gacka valley in lika, inland across the velebit. selce on the vinodol coast - the antic-papic and jellicic lines. karlobag south down the coast under the velebit - the pilipic, uroda, smojver and gerkacs lines, and the archive's deepest generation. klenovica & povile the kalanj villages, on the coast between novi vinodolski and senj - and, it turns out, not where the kalanji are from. house 22 is one house under two village names, and holds 67 people. brinje inland, over the kapela, and the only place on this list nobody has ever searched. the kalanj baptism of 1864 calls the parents brinjensis parochiae ruricolae - country people of the parish of brinje. kalanj, perkovic and boric all appear there. prozor & sumecica the two otocac villages the oldest zubrinic entries name - prozor 46 and 50, sumecica 2 and 24. six people left prozor for new york between 1907 and 1912. port pirie south australia. the zubrinic emigration of about 1884, and the zubrinich spelling. every place, counted every place is a link: it opens the register filtered to the people recorded there. births and deaths of published people carrying one of the eight surnames. spelling variants are collapsed where they are literally the same place; nothing distinct is merged. house numbers are kept, because in frontier registers the house number is the family. q: port pirie one man left senj for a lead-smelting town on the far side of the world, and his name changed on arrival. twenty of his the australian zubrinici, from about 1884 port pirie one man left senj for a lead-smelting town on the far side of the world, and his name changed on arrival. twenty of his descendants are in this tree, and every one of them is a zubrinich. the first of them is joannes / juan / ivan / ive / john zubrinic - a man carried in this tree under five versions of one given name - born 1860 and died 1930 at port pirie, south australia . his eldest recorded child is born there in 1885 , which puts his arrival at about 1884 . from that child onward the surname in the register is zubrinich . not once does it revert. the names → why port pirie port pirie is not a random landfall. smelting began there in 1889 , and it grew into one of the largest lead smelters in the world - heavy, dangerous, continuous work that paid, and that hired men without english. croatians began arriving in south australia from the dalmatian islands in the 1890s , and many of them went to port pirie and broken hill . further groups came with the economic depression in dalmatia and medimurje between 1910 and 1913 , and again after the political unrest of 1922 . the family's later moves confirm the pattern exactly: this tree records zubrinich deaths at broken hill and whyalla - the silver-lead mine and the steelworks. they followed the metal. an anomaly worth flagging. ivan's birthplace is entered as "senj, split-dalmatia, croatia" . senj is in lika-senj county, not split-dalmatia; this is an automated place-match error, and it matters because it is the kind of thing that later gets read as evidence of dalmatian origin. open questions → the australian records in turns up a second, entirely separate emigration: to youngstown, johnstown and brooklyn , and a kalanj emigration to the mining towns of colorado, michigan and illinois. nobody in this family knew about any of it, and the records were never scarce - they were simply never looked for, because one spelling was searched and the other was not. the other emigration → added 13 september 2026 nor only to south australia every one of the 21 australians above is in south australia or, later, at broken hill . that is the whole australian story this archive has told. queensland's own historical index was searched for the first time on 13 september 2026, and it holds one zubrinich. stanley joseph zubrinich married joanna marian josephine clowes in queensland on 15 november 1947 - registration 1947/b/15067 . he is not in this tree, and no stanley joseph is. a candidate, not a relative. nothing here shows how he joins. but two things make him worth the next hour somebody spends. the surname is vanishingly rare , and the anglicised -ich ending is the specific spelling this family adopted on arrival at port pirie and never once reverted from - so a zubrinich in australia is far more likely to be one of these than to be a separate landing. and the given name is the family's: a stanley was born at port pirie in 1896 and died there in 1897, and these are people who re-used the names of children they lost. a stanley joseph marrying in 1947 would have been born around the 1920s, which is exactly the generation of terrence joseph (1924) and maurice william (1922). his marriage certificate would name his parents and settle it. the nulls are worth recording with it. queensland's register covers births to 1926, marriages to 1951 and deaths to 1996, and across that span it holds no zubrinic , no blazevic and no subrinich . the three blazevich entries are a queensland household of thomas bogin blazevich, who married jane chambers in 1940, and are unconnected to anyone here. added 14 september 2026 · find a grave the graves, and who lies in them together this archive had never used a cemetery index. find a grave holds 72 zubrinich memorials and not one of them is in croatia - q: prpic bunjevci of the senj mountain, recorded for four generations at a single house number. krivi put prpic bunjevci of the senj mountain, recorded for four generations at a single house number. 155 published people 1820 earliest birth year 9 distinct spellings in the tree krivi put 136 thirty-five people in this tree are born at krivi put 136 . the baptismal register - kept in latin - has antonija as entry 51: nata 12 may 1859 , baptisata 15 may , antonia perpic, legit. , daughter of the spouses joannes and lucia perpic , locus domicilii krivi put n⁰ 136 , godparents lucas tomljanovic and anna tomljanovic, daughter of andreas . house numbers are how frontier registers identify a family, and a settled household can hold one for a century. they were frontier households too the fuller of the two scans of antonija's 1859 baptism carries a conditio column the other crop omits, and the word in it is confiniar. - confiniarii . nor is it one household: on the same opening the perpic , tomljanovic and butkovic families are all entered the same way. so krivi put was a military frontier village , exactly as otocac was. this archive had the bunjevac settlement and the zubrinic confiniarii as separate facts and never joined them. it came out of re-reading a document filed as a duplicate. the page proves the village read the other entries on the same opening and the bunjevac claim stops being an inference from place-names and becomes an observation. the surnames baptised at krivi put in the summer of 1859 are perpic, tomljanovic, blazevic, sojat, pavelic, vukelic, butkovic - and krmpotic , the clan the whole settlement is named for. every child is entered against a house number: n⁰ 4, 14, 15, 18, 23, 41, 51, 54, 58, 61, 72, 79, 81, 82, 136. prpic or perpic the tree writes it prpic 83 times, perpic 19, perpic 16, prpic 8 , once as perpich , and once - with admirable honesty - as "papic or perpic" . antonija is entered under both : "perpic / prpic". this archive treats prpic and perpic as one name , which is a decision, and it is written down as one. where she is buried antonija died at senj on 2 february 1935 and is buried at mirogoj in zagreb - s: Hedviga's second husband was born on Rhodes in 1913, into a Sephardic community that was almost entirely destroyed in 19
q: rhodes hedviga's second husband was born on rhodes in 1913, into a sephardic community that was almost entirely destroyed in 19 santou isaac codron, 1913-1997 rhodes hedviga's second husband was born on rhodes in 1913, into a sephardic community that was almost entirely destroyed in 1944 - and he died in south africa in 1997. how he came to be alive to marry her is the most interesting unanswered question in this archive. the tree records him plainly and briefly: santou (shemtov) isaac codron , born 13 september 1913 at rhodes , died 16 april 1997 in south africa of cardio-respiratory arrest, married to hedviga about 1973 . that is every fact held on him. each one opens onto a large history. shemtov - shem tov , "good name" - is a sephardic given name, and codron is a known rhodes jewish surname. he was, on the face of the record, a rhodesli . 23 july 1944 what happened to the community he was born into rhodes held a sephardic jewish community that had been there since the fifteenth century, speaking judeo-spanish - the language their ancestors carried out of spain in 1492. in the quarter called la djuderia it was still, in 1944, a living world. on 20 july 1944 the ss ordered the island's jews to assemble for a document check. 1,615 people from rhodes , together with 94 from kos , were packed into the cargo holds of livestock ships, taken to the greek mainland, and put on a train. they arrived at auschwitz on 16 august 1944 after what is generally called the longest deportation journey of the holocaust . about 1,200 were murdered on arrival. roughly 150 survived. santou codron was thirty in july 1944. if he was on rhodes that month, he was almost certainly on that transport - and the odds of walking out of it were about one in eleven. the likelier explanation, and why he probably was not there - because the rhodes jews had been leaving for southern africa for fifty years, and that is exactly where he turns up. rhodesli men began going to africa for work at the end of the nineteenth century; mousa and solomon benatar settled in southern rhodesia in 1895 . emigration accelerated through the 1920s and 1930s, to the belgian congo , southern rhodesia and south africa - for economic reasons first, and from 1938 because of the italian racial laws, rhodes then being italian territory. sephardim from rhodes settled in salisbury , today's harare, and founded a synagogue there in 1932 . in all, close to two thousand jews from rhodes lived in the congo and southern rhodesia between the 1920s and the 1960s. now set hedviga's own movements beside that. she came to south africa from zimbabwe - that is, from rhodesia - in april 1975 , and she is recorded as marrying codron around 1973 , which places the marriage in the rhodesian years. so the meeting has an obvious setting. a croatian woman from senj and a sephardic jew from rhodes, both a long way from home, in the small european society of late-colonial rhodesia - s: Half the town was destroyed in two days. Hedviga was seventeen and living in it, and her aunt lost a husband and two dau
q: senj, 1943 half the town was destroyed in two days. hedviga was seventeen and living in it, and her aunt lost a husband and two dau 7-8 october 1943 senj, 1943 half the town was destroyed in two days. hedviga was seventeen and living in it, and her aunt lost a husband and two daughters that year. this archive had senj as an economic story - a port that the railway killed in 1873 . it is also a war story, and the war reached the family directly. nothing in the family tree says so ; the dates do. what happened italy capitulated on 8 september 1943 , and the italian occupation zone along the adriatic collapsed. senj, with its harbour and its road up to lika, became one of the most important partisan ports on the coast: weapons and war material were concentrated in the town and ships lay in the harbour. on 7 and 8 october 1943 german aircraft bombed the town and the port. 52 killed - 30 local residents and 22 foreigners ~60 civilians recorded seriously or lightly wounded 50% of the town destroyed to its foundations; only about a quarter of buildings still habitable figures from the croatian scholarly literature on the german bombing of senj in 1943. sources → the family in it anka blazevic's household anka blazevic (1893-1953) was ljubomir's sister - hedviga's aunt, and the radnica who worked the floor of the tobacco factory alongside her sister-in-law milka . on 20 november 1919 she married pavao kosina , born at senj on 15 march 1894. pavao kosina b. 15 march 1894, senj - died 8 october 1943 , the second day of the bombing otilija kosina b. 1920 - died 1943 , no day recorded antun kosina b. 1921 - died 2003. a priest : his cross reads vlc. - velecasni , reverend oskar kosina b. 4 september 1922, senj - died 1954, buenos aires neda kosina b. 1924 - died 7 september 1943 , a month before the raid krizan kosina b. 1940 - died 1941, an infant anka outlived them by a decade and died in 1953. confirmed, september 2026 - an inference becomes a document the stone says it outright this page first said pavao kosina was probably one of the thirty, and was careful to add that the date came from the family tree rather than from any record. then his grave was found in the media library. the kosina plot, senj. three portrait medallions below the inscription. ovdje pociva u miru bozjem pavao kosina ✳ 15.iii.1894. · pog. 8.x.1943. nevina zrtva zracnog napadaja na senj u znak sjecanja podize - zahvalna supruga i sinovi "here rests in god's peace pavao kosina, born 15 march 1894, killed 8 october 1943. an innocent victim of the air raid on senj. raised in memory by his grateful wife and sons." pog. is poginuo - killed, the word used for a violent death rather than an ordinary one. the family did not merely record the date; they recorded the cause, and their judgement of it . nevina zrtva - an innocent victim. and one word carries the rest of the story. the stone was raised by supruga i sinovi - his wife and his sons . not his daughters. otilija and neda were both dead by the end of that same year. the plate below also carries krizan (1940-1941), the infant, and anka herself, who outlived them all to 1953. where the kosinas came from a marriage in a front room, 1857 pavao kosina's mother was angelika boras (1857-1902), and the boras reach this archive through her. their own beginning is one of the more human entries in it. senj marriages, 9 february 1857 , entry 52 - caelebs josephus boras , filius denatorum josephi et annae boras natae butvalz - cum vidua maria … in domo privata copulate fuere. ages 32 and 28. they married in a private house , by dispensation of the bishop - a departure from the parish church that usually means illness, urgency or irregularity. he is entered as a bachelor , she as a widow . and they already had three children : ana and anton in 1854, ivan in 1855. angelika follows the marriage , later in 1857. it is a legitimation - a union of some years put right in a front room under episcopal licence. her brother ivan boras (1855-1926) went into the carinska sluzba , the customs service , a state post in a port town; her grandmother's name was anna butvalz , german, as ana untersinger is in the zubrinic line. two german surnames marry into this family in the frontier century, which is what an imperial administration leaves behind. angelika died in 1902 . she did not see her son marry anka blazevic in 1919, and she did not see 1943. what is claimed, and what is not documented german aircraft bombed senj on 7-8 october 1943 , killing 30 local residents and 22 others and destroying about half the town. documented in the tree pavao kosina died on 8 october 1943 . documented that he was one of them - the stone says so. see below. not claimed that otilija (1943, undated) or neda ( 7 september 1943) died in the bombing. neda's date is a month before it - and the day before italy's capitulation. three deaths in one household in one year is not one event until something says it is. what would settle it. the senj death register for 1943 , which would give cause and place for all three; and the published list of the town's bombing victims, which exists in the local historical literature. open questions → where it leaves the rest of the family hedviga was seventeen she was born in senj in 1926 and her children were born there and at crikvenica in 1948, 1951 and 1953 - so she was in the town, or near it, when half of it came down. her brother oto was twenty, and had two years to live . the first version of her page here said she was "fifteen when the war reached the coast". it reached her street. and then argentina her cousin oskar kosina (1922-1954) died at buenos aires . that is the second documented destination of this family after port pirie - and it matches the surname statistics exactly: of the sixty-nine people in the world spelling the name zubrinic , twenty-nine are in argentina , the largest group anywhere. the names → 

s: Senj made this family and then stopped being able to feed it. Every occupation in the record — day labourer, porter, sai
q: senj senj made this family and then stopped being able to feed it. every occupation in the record - day labourer, porter, sai the town the railway went around senj senj made this family and then stopped being able to feed it. every occupation in the record - day labourer, porter, sailor, cigarette-factory hand - is a consequence of one decision taken in 1873. senj sits under the velebit at the head of the senjska draga , where the bura comes off the mountain hard enough to stop traffic. it is one of the oldest towns on the croatian coast, and for four hundred years it was a place of consequence: a free royal town, a bishopric, a habsburg military port, and the home of the uskoks . 1537-1618 the uskoks and nehaj when the ottomans took klis in 1537, its defenders - refugees the slavs called uskoci , "the ones who jumped in" - fell back to senj. the habsburgs put them on the frontier payroll and let them raid. they became, depending on who was writing, a christian bulwark or a pirate confederacy; in practice both, because vienna paid them irregularly and they took the difference out of venetian and ottoman shipping. in 1558 the captain ivan lenkovic built nehaj on the hill above the town, using stone from the churches and monasteries outside the walls so that a besieger would have nothing to shelter behind. it was the uskok headquarters until the uskok war of 1615-18 ended with venice and vienna agreeing to disperse them inland. nehaj still stands over the town, and it is the thing everyone photographs. this archive claims no uskok descent. the uskoks were broken up in 1618 and the earliest person in this tree is born about 1717 - a century later. what the uskok period explains is not the family's blood but the family's place : it is why there was a fortified, garrisoned, habsburg-administered town here at all, and why the empty mountain behind it was about to be settled on purpose. the settlement → the turning point 1873: the railway goes to rijeka senj's whole nineteenth century was built on being the port where the lika highlands met the sea. timber, wool and livestock came down the roads from the interior and went out through senj. then the karlovac-rijeka railway opened in 1873 and did not come here. the traffic followed the rails to rijeka. senj's port trade collapsed, and it never recovered. this is the single most important economic fact in this archive, because the family's recorded work sits directly downstream of it: toma blazevic 1838-1907 nadnicar - day labourer. born at br. 114, smokvica krmpotska ; died at senj and buried there. a man who came off the mountain to a town that had no work left. josip "joso" papic 1857-1939 trhonosa, bremenar, gostionicar - load-carrier, porter, innkeeper. the first two are the same job twice: carrying other people's goods on your back for a fee. the third is what he made of it. ljubomir blazevic 1892-1966 mornar - sailor. born at rijeka , not senj - the family had already followed the work to the port that got the railway. he came back, and died at senj. milka papic 1886-1971 supervisor of workers at the cigarette factory , tvornica duhana , senj. her sister-in-law anka blazevic (1893-1953) was a radnica - a floor worker - at the same factory. a town of incomers, and the register says where from page 107 of the senj baptisms holds eight entries from 1885. four of them - half - record not a mother's trade but the parish she came from . katarina roncevic of jablanac , down the coast katarina stimac of the parish of crnoluska roza babic of the parish of starigrad tonka papic rodj. prpic iz krivogputa - from krivi put this archive already knows antonija prpic is of krivi put, because her 1859 baptism is there. here the senj register says it too - twenty-six years later and a mountain away, a town clerk recording that this woman is not from the town. so the family's arrival in senj was not unusual. it was what senj was. the blazevici coming down from smokvica and the papici from selce are not exceptions to a settled population - they are the population, and the book was recording it in half its entries. the same page gives the fathers' trades: nadcestar (road overseer), bremenar (porter), tezak (labourer), mornar (sailor), with trgovac and postolar among the godparents. what they did → the tobacco factory the habsburg tobacco monopoly was extended to croatia, slavonia and the military frontier by an imperial patent of 20 november 1850 , effective from march 1851, and state tobacco factories followed across the region. senj's was one of them, and for two generations of this family it was the employer of last resort in a town with no port trade - women's work, indoors, waged, and steady in a way that carrying sacks was not. after the second world war the senj factory was liquidated and its cigarette-making machinery was transferred to the tobacco factory at rovinj . the tree records the building's later life exactly: the address is given as ul. stjepana radica 4, 53270 senj , with the note that it "now is a textile factory". and it is why these families met. one page of the senj marriage register for 1918 carries three brides entered as radnica u tvornici duhana - from otocac/sumecica , from krivi put , and from senj . those are the three places this archive comes from. counting milka , her sister-in-law anka , antonija blazevic and ana papic , six women of these families worked that floor. the factory was the institution that brought the mountain villages into the town - and it is a large part of why a blazevic of smokvica, a prpic of krivi put and a zubrinic of otocac end up in one family. unverified here. the senj factory's founding date, size and closure year have not been confirmed from a croatian source by this archive. the monopoly patent and the transfer of machinery to rovinj are documented generally; the specific history of the senj plant is an open question . two days that finished what the railway started 7-8 october 1943 after italy's capitulation senj became one of the most important partisan ports on the adriatic, and german aircraft bombed the town and harbour over two days in october 1943. thirty local residents were killed and about half the town was destroyed to its foundations ; only a quarter of the buildings were still habitable. hedviga was seventeen. her aunt's husband died on the second day. senj, 1943 → and then the boats out a port town with no port sends its people away. this tree records the destinations plainly: port pirie in south australia , where ivan zubrinic went about 1884 and where his descendants still are; buenos aires , where hedviga's cousin oskar kosina died in 1954; and then, two generations later, africa - hedviga to rhodesia and then to johannesburg in april 1975 . september 2026 - the by-name becomes the surname, in two documents this archive has argued for years that papa is a nadimak attached to antic . two senj entries, twenty-eight years apart, show it stop being one. 1 november 1857 - the baptism of ahnentafel 6, in the prose register: anno domini 1857 die 1 nbris. ego joannes tusic , cooperator loci, baptizavi josephum , filium legitimum, romano-catholicum, joannis papa et ejus uxoris mathiae pilipic . levantibus patrinis … ✝ michael stipancic . the date matches the tree to the day, the parents are named, and the godfather signs with a cross . 3 may 1885 - the same man's marriage, entry 5: josip papic, bremenar , of senj, aged 27 - son of «juraj papa, tezak, i matia rodjena pilipic» read them together. the father is joannis papa in 1857 and juraj papa in 1885 - and never antic in either . the son is already papic . the by-name has displaced the surname outright in the parish register by 1857 and hardened into a new surname within one generation , and both halves of that are now documents rather than an argument. the by-names → the marriage also names ahnentafel 7's parents - ivan perpic and luce - which settles ahnentafel 14 and gives 15 her given name from a register.

the catalogue heading is wrong . anyone re-searching by place name will not find it. open questions → the spine: myheritage a single family tree of 15,643 people and 4,777 families , exported as gedcom on 8 september 2026 . it is the structure of this archive and the origin of nearly every date. within it, individual people cite other trees - geni world family tree , defranceski family site , boras web site , grlica web site , janicic , marko karic rodoslov . one export, six archives. this is not a blazevic export - it is the whole tree, covering the defranceski, lerena, taylor, barry, blazevic and booyzen families, and the sibling archives are built from the same file. so a fact contradicted here is contradicted in all of them, and a re-export refreshes all of them at once. checked 10 september 2026: still current, and nothing here depends on a newer one. many notes carry a smartcopy stamp from geni, dated 2014-2017. that records when a record was copied between websites , not when anything was verified. the build strips this boilerplate from the displayed notes and keeps the human prose. statistics and history forebears - surname incidence and density by country and croatian county. built on national registers; port pirie smelter history. used here → croatian scholarship on the german bombing of senj in 1943 ( njemacko bombardiranje senja 1943. ), for the dates, the casualty figures and the proportion of the town destroyed. used here → consulted, and rejected one source this archive will not use an automated surname-origin website was consulted for zubrinic and is not relied on anywhere here . it offers two unrelated etymologies in the same article, places the name in dalmatia when its croatian density is highest in lika-senj, and names a "petar zubrinic, 18th-century croatian ban" who did not exist - the bans of that century were palffy, draskovic, eszterhazy, branyng, batthyany, nadasdy, esterhazy, balassa and erdody. the full check → never consulted, and it shows no death certificate has been obtained for hedviga (johannesburg 2001) or ivan (senj 1995), and no extract for the 1920 senj marriage . no south african or rhodesian immigration file . no yugoslav war victims register search for oto . no mirogoj cemetery record for antonija prpic. these are the next things to do. open questions → until september 2026 this page said that no civil registration document underpinned anything here. that is no longer true - the 1951 birth extract came out of the myheritage media library, where it had been sitting all along, attached to hedviga's profile and absent from the gedcom export.
